# Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Test-first tracer bullet: write the regression tests **before** the fix. Expectations that
target the new behaviour carry `xfail(strict=True)` until the implementation child removes
the marker; expectations that already hold (the conservative failure paths, the
ancestry-not-equality rule) pass before and after, so a failing test can only be failing on
the behaviour under test.

## Goal

As an implementation agent, I want hermetic, deterministic tests that pin the remote-observed
push verdict, so a later change to `finish`'s push-outcome handling can never silently regress
into reporting a landed push as a failure — nor into claiming success for a commit that never
reached `origin/dev`.

## Context

`finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on whether the commit reached
`origin/dev`, so a push interrupted after the remote accepted the ref (timeout, process-group
kill, late non-zero exit) is reported as a failure and the item is reset to `open`. The only
remote check today is the post-*success* ancestry assertion
(`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, `implement.py` L8084), which runs after a push already
claimed success — nothing distinguishes "landed but interrupted" from "never landed". No
existing test simulates the race: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py`,
`tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` all assume the push verdict is truthful.

## Scope

Tests only — no production-code change in this slice. Deliver the failing baselines that the
implementation child turns green, plus the companion tests that prove the preconditions (a
real hermetic push, a reachable bare remote, a real terminal read-back) rather than assuming
them.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — new hermetic suite: probe variants, the three outcomes, sibling-push ancestry.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing interrupted-push coverage; extend where a case belongs there.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push baseline (a retry that lands but is reported as failed).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — reusable `init_bare_remote` / `init_repo` / `add_worktree` / `commit_all` factories; reuse rather than hand-rolling fixtures.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the `FakeGitBoundary` stubbed-boundary harness style for end-to-end `phase_finish` tests.

## Constraints

- **Hermetic:** self-contained bare remote plus clone/worktree under `tmp_path`; never mutate the live checkout's refs, never touch the shared `refs/heads/dev`, no network access.
- **Unambiguous baselines:** pair each new-behaviour `xfail(strict=True)` with a companion that passes before and after, so the preconditions are proven separately instead of being smuggled into the baseline.
- **No hiding failures:** `xfail(strict=True)` only where the expectation targets the not-yet-implemented behaviour.
- **Test execution policy:** no agent-initiated `pytest`/`run_tests.py` invocation outside `/skill:test` (`implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate and the dev-push gate are infrastructure and out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Interrupted push variants are covered by unit tests.** Unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant — `PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, and a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward — and assert the remote verification probe runs before any push failure is reported: it verifies whether the commit being pushed is reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>`), is time-bounded, uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
- **Verified-landed success end-to-end.** An end-to-end hermetic test against a bare remote plus a clone under `tmp_path` — where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short timeout — asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked `verified_after_failure`, the completion comment naming the commit is posted, the existing success-path cleanup runs (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), and the work item is `completed`/`in_review` with the terminal read-back still passing.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are distinguished.** Negative tests — a remote without the commit, and a verification probe that itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error) — assert `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Hermetic regression coverage, ancestry not equality.** The new tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote plus clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation, no network access) and cover an interrupted push that landed, an interrupted push that did not land, a verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted); they fail without the fix (or exercise the new helper directly) and pass with it, reusing the `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories.
data.title: Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).

# Document remote-observed push verdict

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Documentation slice for the remote-observed push verdict. It follows the implementation slice
so it describes the shipped behaviour (the new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` probe, the report
fields, and the three outcomes) rather than a planned one.

## Goal

As an operator or implementation agent reading the finish documentation, I want the three push
outcomes and their recovery paths stated explicitly, so I never retry completed work and never
manually push a commit that is already on `origin/dev`.

## Context

The current "Push timeout" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (L1436) says a
timeout "resets status to `open`" and posts a manual-push comment — that is exactly the false
failure this parent fixes. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` describes `finish`'s behaviour around
L329–L371 but says nothing about a push verdict being verified against the remote.

## Scope

Documentation only: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, and
any code comment the implementation slice leaves inconsistent. No behaviour change.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Push timeout" section (L1436) and the push-failure table entries.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish / push-to-dev guidance (L329–L371).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — doc-hygiene guard to re-run.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — code comments in the push-outcome handlers.

## Constraints

- Describe only behaviour that the implementation slice actually ships; no speculative or aspirational wording.
- Keep the existing document structure and cross-reference style; do not restructure unrelated sections.
- UK English, and no claim that a timeout always resets the item to `open`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Both documentation files describe the remote-observed verdict.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (push timeout / recovery section) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the remote-observed verdict, the three outcomes, and their recovery paths, so a doc review confirms both files describe the new behaviour and no longer state that a timeout always resets the item to `open`. The reference doc's "Push timeout" section (≈ L1436) additionally records the bounded `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`git merge-base --is-ancestor` probe that never runs the pre-push hook or the test suite.
- **`skill/implement/SKILL.md` states the three outcomes and their recovery.** The finish/push-to-dev guidance (≈ L329–L371) states that a `finish` report names which of the three outcomes occurred, that a push the remote verification confirms as landed completes normally (`completed`/`in_review`) rather than being reported as a failure, and that a genuine failure retains the worktree and requires a manual push.
- **Full project test suite passes and all related documentation is updated.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate), and all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries; doc-hygiene tests under `skill/implement/tests/` (e.g. `test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py`) still pass.

## Goal

Restore the `do-not-delegate` guard in `implement.py` automatic parent
recursion. A complete implementation, test suite and docs edit already exist
in the recoverable commit `91c9b44d1` (from the now-deleted subset item
SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876); this child replays that work onto the current tree
rather than re-deriving it.

Provenance: `git show 91c9b44d1` — files
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` (612 lines).
Its base `c818324b1` is an ancestor of `dev`, so it replays cleanly except
for one deliberate adaptation (below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (`skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (`"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking.

- `phase_drive` spawns no session for a guarded child and forwards `guarded_children` for parity with `phase_parent`.

# Implement branch-aware worktree creation

## Goal

Make `phase_start` branch-aware so an existing child branch no longer fails
generically with "Failed to create worktree". The branch is either reused
(identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch) or the operator gets
an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures (`created` / `branch-exists` / `failed` verdicts), with the single `phase_start` call site updated and the source-order assertion in `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` kept satisfied.
- Reuse path: a branch whose tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) the parent branch is fast-forwarded to the parent tip with `git branch -f` and registered with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`); the report sets `reused_branch: true` and `branch_fast_forwarded: true|false`.
- Unsafe path: a branch carrying commits not reachable from the parent branch (or from `origin/<parent_branch>`) is never reset or reused silently; `phase_start` fails with the branch name, the unique-commit count and the exact recovery commands, and resets the item to `open`.
- A branch checked out in another worktree is reported by name and never raced.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Introduce verdict constants + `branch_exists(repo_root, branch)` (via
  `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`) and
  `_branch_reuse_verdict(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `identical` / `fast-forwardable` / `unique-commits`, plus
  `_branch_checked_out_in_other_worktree(repo_root, branch)`.
- Change `git_worktree_add` to return the verdict string; keep the call
  prefix `git_worktree_add(branch,` so existing source-order assertions hold.
- In `phase_start` step 7, when `not resumed` and `branch_exists`: compute the
  verdict, fast-forward when safe, then register the worktree from the
  existing branch; otherwise set `report["success"] = False`,
  `report["stale_branch"] = {branch, unique_commits, recovery_commands}` and
  return after resetting status to `open`.
- Report the decision under `report["steps"]["worktree_branch"]` so `parent`
  and `drive` reports surface why a start reused a branch.

## Constraints

- Never `git branch -f`, `reset` or delete a branch that has commits absent
  from the parent branch — reuse is limited to branches with no unique
  commits.
- Do not weaken the main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, code
  freeze gate, or parent-tracking assertion.
- Preserve `--worktree-path` override semantics and the idempotent worktree
  resume path (`_is_worktree`).
- Re-running `start` after a successful reuse must be idempotent (no second
  branch, no second worktree, no duplicate comment).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add`, new branch helpers, `phase_start` step 7
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` (source-order assertion)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Verdict-returning `git_worktree_add` plus branch state helpers.
- `phase_start` reuse / fast-forward / actionable-error behaviour.
- Green regression tests for the AC3 matrix.

# Implement safe branch cleanup

## Goal

Stop a failed or aborted `start` from poisoning the next `start` with a
orphaned feature branch: clean up the branch this run created, remove the
abandoned branch on `abort` when it is safe to do so, and always report what
was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- The failed-`start` cleanup also removes the worktree registration it created, so no half-created `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` directory survives the failure.
- `phase_abort` discovers the abandoned branch by prefix (`refs/heads/wl-<item-id>-*`) rather than needing the item title, deletes it with `git branch -d` semantics only when it has no unique commits, and reports `branch_removed` / `branch_retained` with the reason and the recovery command.
- A branch that carries commits not reachable from the parent branch or `origin/<parent_branch>` is retained and named in the abort report and comment — never force-deleted.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New `_delete_branch_if_safe(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `{deleted, reason, unique_commits}` with reasons `deleted` / `not-found` /
  `unique-commits` / `checked-out-elsewhere` / `error`; unique-commit count is
  taken against both the local parent branch and `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- New `_discover_item_branches(repo_root, work_item_id)` via
  `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) "refs/heads/wl-<id>-*"`.
- Wrap the post-`git worktree add` steps of `phase_start` so a failure after
  creation removes the worktree (guarded by `_remove_worktree`) and then
  deletes the branch this run created, reporting
  `report["cleanup"] = {worktree_removed, branch_removed, reason}`.
- In `phase_abort`, after the worktree removal and before
  `_restore_repo_state`, delete each discovered item branch that is safe and
  record the outcome on the abort comment.

## Constraints

- No blind `git branch -D`: deletion is only reached when the unique-commit
  count is zero, and a branch checked out in another worktree is never
  touched.
- Cleanup failures are logged and reported, never fatal to `abort`.
- Idempotent: a second abort finds no branch and reports `not-found` without
  error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_delete_branch_if_safe`, `_discover_item_branches`, `phase_start` post-create failure path, `phase_abort`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite".
- Blocked by "Implement branch-aware worktree creation" (shares the branch
  helpers and must not conflict on the `phase_start` failure path).

## Deliverables

- Guarded branch deletion helper and item-branch discovery.
- Failed-start cleanup of the worktree and the branch it created.
- Abort-time branch removal/retention reporting.

# Replace bare `except`-`pass` with exception logging in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` contains a `try`-`except` block in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` that catches all exceptions from `git for-each-ref` and silently passes. This hides diagnostic information about why feature branch resolution failed, making it harder to debug merge-gate issues in production.

## Users

- **Agent auditors**: When the merge gate fails to resolve feature branches, the silent pass means the failure reason is lost — the audit proceeds but with silently missing evidence.
- **Maintainers debugging audit failures**: Without exception details, diagnosing why a specific work item's branch refs could not be resolved requires reproducing the exact failure conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The bare `except Exception: pass` in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` (feature-branch resolution section, ~line 11799) is replaced with a `print` to `sys.stderr` that reports the issue ID and exception details, while retaining fail-open semantics.
2. The `noqa: S110` directive is removed (the bare pass no longer exists).
3. The `noqa: BLE001` directive is retained (the exception is still swallowed to stay fail-open).
4. The change is a single-function edit (replacing `pass` with a `print` call and binding the exception via `as exc`).
5. No functional behaviour change — the merge gate still fails open when ref resolution fails.

## Impact

Audit agents can now see *why* feature-branch resolution failed, improving debuggability of merge-gate evidence gaps.

## Constraints

- Must use the same `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` pattern already established in this file.
- Must not change any return values, function signature, or upstream callers.
- Must not introduce any new dependencies or imports.

## Existing state

```python
except Exception:  # noqa: S110, BLE001 -- best-effort; never fail the gate on ref resolution
    pass
```

The surrounding function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` resolves feature branches and commit SHAs for merge-gate verification. It is called by the merge-gate verification code which already prints success/failure diagnostics to stderr.

## Desired change

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- best-effort; never fail the gate on ref resolution
    print(
        f"Merge gate: ref resolution for {issue_id} failed — "
        f"git for-each-ref error: {exc}",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
```

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Single exception handler edit in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`

## Related work

- Multiple similar S110 items completed in `audit_runner.py` (SA-0MS3ATEOP005DRAD line 1039, SA-0MS3ATFSJ007GHRB line 1678, SA-0MS3ATGCE002WE91 line 1805).
- The same S110 pattern appears elsewhere in the codebase addressed in separate items.

## Appendix

- Q: What logging pattern to use? — Answer: `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` consistent with existing merge-gate output at line ~12553. Source: codebase scan of audit_runner.py stderr patterns.

finding is at line 183 — the `git rev-parse HEAD` probe in
`TestExecutionWorktree.test_creates_detached_worktree_at_origin_dev`, whose

refactor marker in the module header (`REFACTOR-SA-0MWD28UYZ00255LX`) stays until

  `git rev-parse HEAD` probe, currently line 183) passes `check=` explicitly —
  `check=False`, preserving current behaviour (the return code is intentionally

The audit-skill test tree lints clean again — the PLW1510 finding and its
auto-generated refactor marker are gone, with no behaviour change to the
worktree-isolation tests.

## Constraints

- Behaviour-neutral change only: do not add return-code assertions where none
  existed; the probe's `stdout` is the only consumed output.

  already pass explicit `check` (`check=False` in `_git_runner`; `check=True`

# Problem Statement

Ruff rule `RUF059` ("Unpacked variable ... is never used") flags three names
bound by the tuple unpack on line 118 of `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`:
`mode`, `uid` and `gid`. The work item names only `mode` because it was the
first diagnostic reported, but one fix at that line clears all three.

# Users

- **Test maintainer / any developer running ruff on this repo**: wants the lint
  output for the test suite to be trustworthy, so a real finding is not buried
  under dead bindings in a test that is otherwise clean.

Example user story: *As a developer running ruff over `tests/`, I want
`tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` to report no unused-binding findings, so I
can treat a red lint run as a genuine regression.*

# Acceptance Criteria

1. The tuple unpack on line 118 of `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` no longer
   binds unused names, so `ruff check --select RUF059 tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`
   reports zero findings for that line (covers all three reported names:
   `mode`, `uid`, `gid`).
2. Test behaviour is unchanged: `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines` still
   asserts the six-field count (`type path mode uid gid age`) and the ≥1-day
   age threshold, and `age` still carries the value of `fields[5]`.
3. Validation: `pytest tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` (run through the test
   skill) passes with the change.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Impact

Developers running lint over the test suite get a clean RUF059 signal from this
file again, so a genuine unused-binding regression elsewhere is no longer
masked by known noise here.

# Constraints

- Single-line change inside `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines`; no
  behavioural change and no assertion may be added, removed or weakened.
- The field-count assertion (`len(fields) == 6`) and the age parsing/`>= 86400`
  check must stay exactly as they are.
- Out of scope (see Risks): strengthening the test to validate `mode`/`uid`/
  `gid` values, despite the docstring's "sane values" claim — that is a
  behavioural change to the test, not a lint fix.
- Do not remove the `REFACTOR-SA-0MWDV1YYV007K5EA` marker comment at the top of
  the file: markers are the refactor skill's duplicate-filing guard, and the
  precedent item (SA-0MWDV1XHW005Y6J5) left its own marker in place.
- Rust/ruff version: the diagnostic is reproducible with the ruff available in
  this environment (`ruff check --select RUF059`, 3 findings at line 118).

# Existing state

```python
        fields = line.split()
        rule_type, _ = fields[0], fields[1]   # line 100: F841 already fixed
        ...
        _, _, mode, uid, gid, age = fields    # line 118: RUF059 x3
```

Only `age` is used downstream (the age-threshold assertion). `mode`, `uid` and
`gid` are bound and never read; the surrounding comment
`# AC1: age >= 1 day; ...` confirms `age` is the only intended consumer.

# Desired change

```python
        age = fields[5]
```

Rationale: mirrors the file's existing indexing style one screen above
(`rule_type, _ = fields[0], fields[1]`), keeps the field-order comment
(`type path mode uid gid age`) truthful, and removes all three dead bindings in
one edit.

Alternative considered and rejected: `_, _, _, _, _, age = fields` — correct
but noisier than the indexing form already used in the same function.

The stale RUF059 marker comment at the top of the file is left untouched (see
Constraints).

# Key Files

- `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` — line 118, single-line refactor inside
  `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines`; the test body and assertions are
  otherwise untouched.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: the item's "line 100" refers to the file state at scan time;
  the diagnostic is now at line 118 after intervening commits. The marker
  comment `# <!-- REFACTOR-SA-0MWDV1YYV007K5EA ... -->` in the file header
  confirms the identity, so line-number drift is not a blocker.
- **Risk (scope creep)**: the test docstring claims "sane values" but only age
  is validated. Tempting to add mode/uid/gid assertions while touching the
  line; deliberately excluded — record as a follow-up work item if wanted.
- **Risk (behavioural drift)**: replacing the unpack with `fields[5]` silently
  depends on field order; mitigated by keeping the field-order comment and the
  existing six-field assertion, and by AC2.
- **Risk (conflict)**: SA-0MWDV20G7008ZORK edits a different hunk (~line 167,
  `subprocess.run` `check` argument) of the same file — no merge conflict
  expected.

# Related work

- **SA-0MWDV1XHW005Y6J5** (completed) — same file, F841 unused local `path`;
  established the `_`/indexing convention and the description structure reused
  here.
- **SA-0MWDV20G7008ZORK** (open, stage `idea`) — same file, `subprocess.run`
  without explicit `check` (PLW1510); another linter fix in the same test.
- **SA-0MW2QEZBG009I3AI** — original item that introduced
  `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` and `scripts/pi-test-tmp.conf`.

No questions asked — the seed context plus repository search was sufficient to
draft a complete brief.

Research summary: `ruff check --select RUF059 tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`

# Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Problem statement

A contended host aborts a green unit stage with exit 124 and a diagnostic that (a) describes only
the browser failure mode and (b) prints the **elapsed** time in the sentence that reads as the
**bound**, so an operator cannot tell contention from a genuine hang without opening the cache
entry and re-deriving the numbers by hand.

## Users

- **Release producer** (primary): "When a release aborts in the unit stage I want the log to tell
  me the host was at load 38 on 16 cores and the stage ran 312 s against a 300 s bound, so I retry
  instead of bisecting a green suite."
- **Release producer on an idle host**: "When the unit stage aborts at load 0.4 against a 300 s
  bound, I want the diagnostic to point at a synchronous loop in test/engine code, not at
  `requestAnimationFrame`."
- **CI operator on a small host**: "I want the bound to stay an explicit, overridable number so a
  4-core runner is not handed a bound calibrated for a 16-core workstation."

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Existing state (verified in this intake pass, 2026-11-14)

All line numbers verified against the TCE checkout at `main` @ `70b4981f`.

- **The diagnostic takes only the elapsed time.** `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` at
  `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221` builds the line
  `[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within ${elapsedSecs}s` — the bound (`timeoutMs`) is
  never passed in, so the printed number is elapsed wall time wearing the bound's clothes. This is
  the conflation the ACs call out.
- **Two of three hang messages have the defect.** `listHangMessage` (line 237, pre-flight
  `vitest list`) is the same shape; its bound is the constant `LIST_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`
  (line 217). The third message, the coverage-preflight fallback at line 492, already prints the
  *bound* (`Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)`) — so the codebase is inconsistent rather than uniformly
  wrong, and the fix should unify all three on one shape.
- **Both inputs are already in scope at the call sites.** `runVitestProcess` owns `opts.timeoutMs`
  (the timer at line 1173) and returns `elapsedSecs` (line 1184); the two abort paths
  (`runVitestAsync` line 1214, `runVitestListAsync` line 1246) therefore have bound *and* elapsed
  in hand — the work is threading them into the message plus adding stage and load.
- **Stage is implicit, not first-class.** Nothing in the runner models a stage: `--project unit`
  and `--project browser` are forwarded argv from `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` and `:96`. A stage
  value must either be threaded from the caller or derived from the forwarded args, and it must
  cover the pre-flight `vitest list` too (which forwards the same args).
- **The header comment is already stale.** `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:59` says "5 min for unit
  (nominal <2 min)"; the measured worst green unit stage is 217 s — 72 % of the 300 s bound, not
  "<2 min". The rationale cannot be corrected without the measured baseline being recorded beside
  it, which is why the documentation AC is in scope rather than cosmetic.
- **The outer budget has *zero* slack today, not 4–7 min.** `.pi/test-config.json` sets
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, applied by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:4551`
  (`args.timeout or suite_timeout_per_command(...) or 600`) to the **single** `npm --silent test`
  command that runs the whole of `run-ci-tests.sh`. Today's stage bounds already sum to
  **300 + 1200 = 1500 s — exactly the outer bound** — and that sum excludes the terminology guard,
  the browser-env pre-check, both `vitest list` pre-flights, the shell orchestration, and the
  (unbounded) Tutorial E2E stage. The 4–7 min of headroom in the original AC is measured against
  the *nominal 18–21 min runtime*, not against the sum of bounds, so it does not cover a raise.
  Any raised or scaled unit bound therefore **must** raise `timeoutPerCommand` in the same change
  (e.g. a 600 s floor ⇒ 1800 s of stage bounds ⇒ outer ≈ 2100–2400 s).
- **An over-budget command is reported separately from a hang.** `run_tests.py` emits the
  `suite_timeout` notice (`NOTICE_SUITE_TIMEOUT`, lines 240 / 3247) — the outer and inner bounds
  must not become confusable in the abort log.
- **The test seam pattern already exists.** `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (1353
  lines) injects runners, `binPath` and `killGraceMs`; `runVitestProcess` takes an injectable
  `opts` bag. The load average and core count should follow that same injection style.

## Desired change

1. One shared hang-diagnostic builder that always prints **stage, configured bound, elapsed wall
   time, the delta over the bound, host load average at abort and core count** — used by the run
   abort, the pre-flight `vitest list` abort and the coverage-preflight fallback.
2. Stage-appropriate guidance: the `requestAnimationFrame` / undestroyed `Phaser.Game` /
   "run one file under `--project browser`" paragraph is browser-only; a unit-stage abort instead
   points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code. The pre-flight gets the abbreviated form.
3. A unit-stage bound derived as **hybrid**: a raised static floor (justified against the measured
   baseline) plus load-aware scaling from the sampled 1-min load average relative to core count,
   clamped to a finite ceiling, still overridable with `--timeout-ms`.
4. A corrected outer budget (`.pi/test-config.json`) and a corrected rationale in the
   `run-ci-tests.sh` header and the TCE hang-timeout docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` /
  `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time,
  the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention
  is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry. All three hang messages
  (run abort, pre-flight `vitest list` abort, coverage-preflight fallback) share one builder, so the
  current elapsed-as-bound wording at `hangTimeoutMessage`/`listHangMessage` is gone and bound,
  elapsed, stage and load are rendered identically everywhere.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound) **plus load-aware scaling** of the bound from the
  sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**; the bound
  remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`), and `--timeout-ms` still wins over the computed
  bound.
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout — today the bounds already sum to exactly
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` (300 + 1200) with zero slack, so raising or scaling an inner bound
  either adjusts `.pi/test-config.json` in the same change or documents, with the arithmetic, why
  it still fits.
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline (88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149,
  206, 217 s) are recorded in the `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` and `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  header comments — replacing the falsified "5 min for unit (nominal <2 min)" — and in the TCE
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
- The release gate documents the behaviour on this repo's side: `docs/dev/release-tests.md` gains a
  short "hang abort vs host contention" note stating that a stall is reported as exit 124 with the
  stage/bound/elapsed/load diagnostic, and that a contended-host abort is never auto-retried and
  must be re-run once the host is quiet.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; the
  computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average and core count are injected through a
  test seam and are never read from the real host; cases cover an idle host (floor applies), a
  loaded host (scaling applies), and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus a browser-stage message
  containing no unit-stage guidance and vice versa.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor. `os.loadavg()` is meaningless on Windows — the runner must degrade to the static floor
  there rather than compute a bogus scale.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average or core count in a test; sample it
  behind an injectable seam (the `runVitestProcess` `opts` bag / injected-runner pattern already in
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`).
- **Log noise budget.** The per-attempt `[vitest-runner] ... attempts=N status=S outcome=...` line
  is parsed by release-gate tooling and by `run_tests.py`'s notice classification — the new
  diagnostic enriches the `[hang-timeout]` block and must not break the `[vitest-runner]` line's
  shape.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption.** Load average at abort is sampled *after* the kill, from the parent runner
  process; it is an indicator of contention during the run, not a measurement integrated over it.
  If a more faithful signal (per-attempt max load) turns out cheap to capture, that is an
  implementation choice for the plan, not a new AC.

## Key Files (predicted)

- **Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here)**
  - `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — `hangTimeoutMessage` (line 221) / `listHangMessage`
    (line 237) / the fallback at line 492 unified into one stage-aware builder; load-average +
    core-count sampling seam; hybrid bound derivation (floor + load scale + ceiling) around
    `DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (line 188) and `parseRunnerArgs`' `--timeout-ms` (line 322).
  - `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — unit stage `--timeout-ms` (line 92) raised to the new floor;
    header rationale (line ~51–59) corrected against the measured baseline.
  - `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — diagnostic-content assertions and
    floor/scaling/ceiling cases with an injected load average and core count.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
  - `.pi/test-config.json` — `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` adjusted in the same change as any raised
    unit bound (see the outer-budget AC).
- **This repo (framework)**
  - `docs/dev/release-tests.md` — new "hang abort vs host contention" note (66-line file;
    "How the merge is gated on success" / "Re-running after a fix" are the natural anchors).
  - `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — gate log surface / comments (~line 340–356)
    if the abort is to be surfaced distinctly from a red suite.
  - `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `timeoutPerCommand` handling (line 1488/4551) and the
    `suite_timeout` notice (line 240/3247); read-only unless the outer/inner distinction needs to
    appear in its output.

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** (TCE, completed) — the project-coverage gate whose fail-closed behaviour
  must be preserved.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this
  brief; measured evidence and the evidence corrections (retry log shows a producer-review block,
  not a green retry; load 35–42 is an observation, not a log) carry over.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate design this work hardens.
- Sibling item: **SA-0MWEURY420040OMD** (this repo, `intake_complete`) — the green-cache-entry
  resume path; keeps a unit-stage abort from forcing a full re-run of an unchanged tree.
  Complementary, not sequential.
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** (this repo, completed) — browser-suite contention: two concurrent full
  suites starve each other and vitest runs were SIGKILLed (137) or **hung (124)** at load ~8–12 on
  16 cores. That is the root cause of the collision this item diagnoses; the concurrency ceiling
  change fixed the supply side, this item fixes what the operator is told when it happens anyway
  (three concurrent suites + a Monte-Carlo sweep is not something a semaphore can ration away).
- **SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL** (this repo, open, `idea`) — the release gate discards the runner JSON, so
  `merge-dev-to-main.sh` cannot say why the suite gate failed (`slot_busy` vs `killed` vs red).
  Same file, adjacent concern, different axis (runner-result consumption, not the hang diagnostic);
  not a blocker either way, but the two touch `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` and
  whichever lands second should rebase its log-surface edit on the other rather than reworking it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (bound strategy: A static raise / B load-aware only / C hybrid) — ANSWERED: C (hybrid).**
  Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment on that
  item): "1. C". Agent recommendation (adopted): C. Research: TCE `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  bounds at lines 56/92/96; `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` line 816 ("full suite takes 18–21 minutes"); measured green TCE unit stages
  from `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` — 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst
  217 s on 2026-11-11 17:37); no load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today.
- **Q2 (resume-path scope) — ANSWERED: B (split; framework item).** Answered by producer: "2. B".
  Tracked in the sibling item created alongside this one.
- **Duplicate check** — searched `wl search "hang timeout vitest retry"` (TCE) and this repo's
  items: the browser-stage precedent (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) is completed and does not cover the
  unit-stage bound, the diagnostics content, or the resume path; no duplicate found.
- **Re-intake verification (2026-11-14, Map, SA-0MWEURUYL004I470) — no new questions asked.** The
  brief was re-verified against the trees rather than re-interviewed; every claim above now carries
  a file:line anchor. Findings that changed the brief: (a) the diagnostic's defect is exactly
  `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs)` printing elapsed time as the bound (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221`);
  (b) a third hang message at line 492 already prints the bound, so the fix unifies rather than
  corrects uniformly; (c) the `run-ci-tests.sh:59` rationale "5 min for unit (nominal <2 min)" is
  falsified by the measured 217 s worst green stage; (d) the outer budget has **zero** slack today
  (300 + 1200 = the 1500 s `timeoutPerCommand`), so the original AC's "~4–7 min headroom" was
  measured against nominal runtime and does not cover a raise — the AC now states the arithmetic;
  (e) `os.loadavg()` portability and the `[vitest-runner]` log-shape stability were added as
  constraints; (f) `docs/dev/release-tests.md` named as the framework-side documentation target.
  Issue type (`feature`) and priority (`high`) re-confirmed; no operator input required.
## Plan (2026-11-14, Map — `/skill:plan`)

**Effort:** Medium (PERT expected 48.7 h, recommended 70.7 h) · **Risk:** Medium (score 11/25,
probability 2.1 × impact 5) · **Approval gate:** not requested (the gate requests approval only
for Extra Large **and** High/Severe). Six children, test/verification first in creation order.

### Design decisions the plan owns

- **D1 — Implementation stays in place in TCE.** The bounded runner remains
  `Tableau-Card-Engine: scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, tracked by this item. Rationale: the
  runner is a Node/TS module invoked by TCE's `npm test` and inherited by consuming game repos
  through their TCE pin, its 1353-line test suite lives beside it, and the framework has no TS
  distribution path for `skill/` scripts. Lifting it into `skill/test/` would need a new
  cross-repo packaging mechanism and would split the runner from its tests, for no gain. The
  diagnostic **and** the bound computation therefore live in exactly one file.
- **D2 — `--timeout-ms` remains a strict, verbatim override** (parent AC3: "`--timeout-ms` still
  wins"). Consequence: the shell must stop pinning the unit bound, otherwise the hybrid bound can
  never apply. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` therefore **drops** `--timeout-ms 300000` from the unit
  stage (the runner's hybrid bound applies) and **keeps** the explicit browser bound
  (`--timeout-ms 1200000`). This intentionally differs from the Key Files hint "unit stage
  `--timeout-ms` raised to the new floor" — a pinned unit bound and load-aware scaling cannot
  both hold; the floor is expressed as the runner constant instead.
- **D3 — Hybrid bound formula.** Static floor **600 s** (2.8× the worst measured green unit stage
  of 217 s, 2× the old 300 s bound); finite ceiling **1200 s** (equal to the browser bound);
  scaling `factor = clamp((load1m / cpuCount) / 0.75, 1, 2)` so `bound = clamp(600 s × factor,
  600 s, 1200 s)` — the floor applies at ≤0.75 load/core, the ceiling at ≥1.5 load/core (e.g. 24
  load on 16 cores). Load is sampled **before** the stage starts (to size the bound) and **at
  abort** (for the diagnostic, per the intake assumption), through one injected seam; on Windows
  the load is unavailable and the floor applies.
- **D4 — Outer budget.** Worst case = unit 1200 + browser 1200 + two `vitest list` pre-flights
  240 + terminology/env pre-checks and orchestration ≈ 60 ⇒ **`.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand: 2700`** (was 1500, which already had zero slack). Accepted trade-off: a
  genuine hang can now take up to ~45 min to abort instead of ~25 min — the deliberate price of
  not aborting green stages on a contended host, and the diagnostic prints the bound so the
  generosity is visible. (A 900 s ceiling with `timeoutPerCommand: 2400` was the smaller-footprint
  alternative; rejected because 900 s is only 4.1× the worst measured stage and the incident ran
  under sustained load ≥2/core.)
- **D5 — Log shape is frozen.** The `[hang-timeout]` block is enriched; the
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=…` line and the `suite_timeout` notice keep their
  exact shape (release-gate tooling and `run_tests.py` notice classification parse them).
- **D6 — `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` is not touched.** Its log surface is
  owned by SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL (runner JSON discarded); this item only documents the gate
  behaviour in `docs/dev/release-tests.md`.

### Feature breakdown (creation order = test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Slice | Parent ACs |
| - | ----- | ---- | ----- | ---------- |
| 1 | Verify hang diagnostics and gate budget (SA-0MWFX7VVX002HF1Q) | task | verification (runs last) | AC7, AC8, AC10 |
| 2 | Injectable host contention sampler seam (SA-0MWFX7ZFO009YE0Y) | task | test-first seam | AC1/AC3 inputs, AC8 |
| 3 | Stage-aware unified hang diagnostic builder (SA-0MWFX836K006QWEH) | feature | diagnostic end-to-end | AC1, AC2 |
| 4 | Hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound (SA-0MWFX86ZY0000WVR) | feature | bound end-to-end | AC3, AC7 |
| 5 | Unit bound wiring and outer gate budget (SA-0MWFX8A7I00883VQ) | feature | shell wiring + budget | AC4, AC5 |
| 6 | Document hang baseline, rationale and contention (SA-0MWFX8D8X007PH6Y) | docs | TCE + framework + wiki docs | AC5, AC6, AC9 |

**Parent AC legend** (in description order): AC1 diagnostic content + single builder · AC2
stage-appropriate guidance · AC3 hybrid bound (floor + scaling + ceiling, override wins) · AC4
inner bounds consistent with the outer budget · AC5 rationale + baseline in code headers and TCE
docs · AC6 framework `docs/dev/release-tests.md` note · AC7 hang semantics unchanged · AC8
deterministic tests with injected load/cores · AC9 all related docs · AC10 full suite green.

### Sequencing and vertical slices

Each implementation child is a vertical slice (code + tests + its own header/doc comment), not a
horizontal layer: the sampler seam lands first with its tests, then the diagnostic slice, then
the bound slice, then the wiring/budget slice, then the documentation slice, then the
cross-cutting verification. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it if
the previous slice changed a name or a number (e.g. the derivation's signature, the final
`timeoutPerCommand`).

**Cross-repo:** children 2–6 edit the TCE checkout (`~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`, prefix
`CG`) on a `dev`-based branch — commit messages name this item (`SA-0MWEURUYL004I470`) and the
hash is recorded here; child 6 also edits `docs/dev/release-tests.md` in this repo.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14 — Initial decomposition (6 children, 8 dependency edges), design decisions D1–D6,
  effort/risk estimate (Medium/Medium at intake stage) and AC→child traceability recorded.

- **Planning session (2026-11-14, Map, `/skill:plan`) — no new producer questions asked.** The
  intake brief already carried a verified existing state (file:line anchors) and the producer's
  Q1 = C (hybrid) answer, and it explicitly delegated the in-place-vs-lift design decision to the
  plan, so planning recorded decisions D1–D6 instead of re-interviewing. Notable resolution: the
  brief's Key Files hint "unit stage `--timeout-ms` raised to the new floor" is **not**
  implementable alongside AC3's "`--timeout-ms` still wins" — a pinned unit bound makes the
  load-aware scaling inert — so D2 drops the unit pin in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` and expresses
  the floor as a runner constant. Concrete numbers chosen against the measured baseline: floor
  600 s, ceiling 1200 s, scaling `clamp((load1m/cores)/0.75, 1, 2)`, `timeoutPerCommand` 1500 →
  2700. Effort/risk: Medium / Medium (PERT expected 49.6 h, recommended 71.6 h; risk score
  10/25) — below the approval gate (Extra Large **and** High/Severe), so no approval pause was
  raised.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWEURY420040OMD** – Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a hang abort resumes (in-progress)
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** – Browser suite contention: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 lets two full suites starve each other (137 kills / 124 hangs) (completed)

# Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a unit-stage hang abort resumes

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release, I want a unit-stage hang abort to **not** force a full 20+ minute
re-run when the tree is unchanged: the gate should resume from a green cached full-suite entry
within the cache TTL instead of re-executing the whole suite.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The TCE v0.1.24 release gate aborted in the unit stage with a 300 s hang bound (exit 124; no
failing test — host contention, load 35–42 on 16 cores). The per-repo test cache is keyed on
command + git state with a 2 h TTL; the hang **overwrites** the cache entry for that state with
`exit_code: 124`, so a retry on the same tree re-runs every stage from scratch. The release gate
runs `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on the merged dev→main tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hang/abort result (exit `124` from the bounded vitest runner, or any non-zero abort that
  produced no parsable test results) does **not** destroy a green cache entry for the same tree
  state: when a valid green entry exists for the requested command+state within TTL, the cached
  green verdict is served even if a later aborted run wrote to the same key, and the abort is
  still reported (the gate must never *silently* accept an abort as green).
- The resume path is functional end-to-end: re-running the release gate against an unchanged tree
  (same git state, within TTL) after a unit-stage abort consumes the preserved green full-suite
  entry instead of re-executing `npm --silent test`, with the cache TTL gate intact.
- The release gate documents the resume procedure: `run_tests.py`/cache behaviour and the
  operator-visible statement ("the tree is unchanged within TTL — re-run resumes green") are
  described in this repo's release-gate docs and in `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
  comments; no green-entry destruction happens on abort.
- A failure or changed tree still executes and stores freshly — the preservation never masks a red
  run, a changed git state, or an expired TTL: cache behaviour for abort entries is covered by
  tests in this repo (`tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` alongside
  `skill/test_cache.py` / `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A contended-host abort stops costing a full re-run: the producer retries the release and the gate
resumes from the green entry for the unchanged tree, holding the green verdict while the abort is
still surfaced.

## Constraints

- **Never mask a genuine failure.** A preserved green entry is served only for the same command +
  git state within TTL; any tree change, red verdict, or TTL expiry forces a fresh run.
- **Green-first, but loud.** Returning the preserved green entry must be paired with a clear
  notice that the *aborted* run is being satisfied from the earlier green entry (operator
  visibility), not a silent acceptance of exit 124.
- **Follow the existing cache contract.** Keying, git-state fingerprinting, `scope` / `test_type`
  namespacing and the state-changed quarantine in `test_cache.py` are unchanged; this item only
  refines what a hang/abort writes.
- **Cross-repo consumers.** TCE's audit/release flows consume `query_cached()`; their
  expectations (read-only, verdicts only for matching state) must not regress.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` (this repo — installed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py`) —
  store/lookup semantics for hang/abort (exit 124) entries; green-entry preservation; TTL
  unchanged.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_cached`/`query_cached` usage, abort-result reporting.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — full-suite gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81),
  resume documentation/behaviour.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `query_cached` consumer; must still reject partial/abort
  entries as full-suite evidence.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — coverage for abort-vs-green
  preservation in this repo's test suite.
- `docs/dev/release-tests.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`
  — release-gate / cache documentation to update with the resume procedure.
- Cross-repo (TCE, tracked here): `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout / § Test Configuration —
  document the resume path for TCE release operators.

## Related work

- **Sibling item: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit bound** (created alongside
  this one) — prevents the abort in the first place; this item makes the residual abort cheap to

# Report summary line should match the skill that produced it

## Problem statement

Every end-of-session report closes with a hardcoded `✅ Ready to ship` (green) or `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) Conclusion line, no matter which skill produced the report. All 16 skills that call `render_report.py` — plan, intake, implement, audit, test, ship, refactor, cleanup, triage, etc. — say "Ready to ship", which is only accurate for the audit/ship skills and actively misleading for the rest (e.g. intake's report claiming the work item is ready to ship before planning has even happened).

## Users

Primary users are the **producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports, and the **agents** whose final message renders the report.

- As a producer, I want the closing line of a report to reflect what the skill actually accomplished, so I can tell at a glance whether a stage genuinely finished.
- As an agent, I want the verdict line I render to be accurate for the skill I ran, so my final message is not misleading.

## Impact

Producers can tell at a glance, from the very last line of any session report, exactly which stage completed (or failed) and what the work item is ready for next — no more generic "Ready to ship" from an intake or plan session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `render_report.py` renders a per-skill summary line on success — plan → "Plan complete", intake → "Intake complete", implement → "Ready for audit", audit → "Ready to ship" (unchanged), and a sensible drafted line for each remaining skill (full mapping in Desired change). Unknown/unmapped `skill_name` falls back to today's "Ready to ship" (backward compatible).
- AC2: The failure line mirrors its skill's success line (e.g. implement → "Not ready for audit", intake → "Intake incomplete"), preserving the red colouring and the closing "This completes the <skill> process for <id> (<title>)." sentence.
- AC3: Every skill that invokes `render_report.py` (all 16 SKILL.md call sites) renders its own line without further per-skill changes — the mapping lives in the renderer keyed by `skill_name` (case-insensitive).
- AC4: Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` docs and the golden-report examples so the documented Conclusion matches the new per-skill behaviour; README/wiki entries referencing the conclusion line are updated.
- AC5: `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` covers the mapping: at least one happy-path per skill or a table-driven parametrised test, one failure-line case, one unknown-skill fallback case, and the existing "Ready to ship" assertions updated to the new expectations.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve colour behaviour (`colour_enabled` auto-detection and `--colour`/`--no-colour` overrides) as-is; only the words change, not the colour logic.
- Keep the Conclusion wording backward compatible: any skill not in the mapping (e.g. future skills) must still get today's "Ready to ship" line rather than erroring.
- Do not alter the header line (`# Completed <skill>`), AC table, or Meta-Data sections — only the Conclusion verdict line(s).

## Existing state

`render_report.py` Conclusion section (lines ~604–618) hardcodes:

- success: `✅ Ready to ship` + "This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title})."
- failure: `🚫 Not ready to ship` + "{Skill} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete."

The `skill_name` parameter is already passed by every caller (16 SKILL.md call sites, verified by grep) and is already used in the header and the closing sentence — only the verdict line ignores it.

## Desired change

Add a per-skill mapping (draft; operator to confirm during review) in `render_report.py`:

| skill_name | success line | failure line |
|---|---|---|
| plan | Plan complete | Plan incomplete |
| intake | Intake complete | Intake incomplete |
| implement | Ready for audit | Not ready for audit |
| audit | Ready to ship | Not ready to ship |
| ship | Released to dev | Release incomplete |
| test | All tests passed | Tests failed/incomplete |
| refactor | Refactor complete | Refactor incomplete |
| cleanup | Cleanup complete | Cleanup incomplete |
| triage | Triage complete | Triage incomplete |
| code-review | Review complete | Review incomplete |
| author-command | Command authored | Command authoring incomplete |
| resolve-pr-comments | PR comments resolved | PR comments incomplete |
| find-related | Related work gathered | Related work search incomplete |
| effort-and-risk | Effort and risk assessed | Effort/risk assessment incomplete |
| machine-hygiene | Hygiene check complete | Hygiene check incomplete |
| agent-log-review | Log review complete | Log review incomplete |
| *(unknown)* | Ready to ship | Not ready to ship |

Failure lines keep the existing explanatory sentence about the incomplete session.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Add the per-skill summary-line mapping and use it for the Conclusion verdict lines (lines ~604–618).
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update "Ready to ship" assertions (~lines 586–1060) and add mapping/failure/fallback coverage.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Update Conclusion examples (golden report shows `✅ Ready to ship`), document the mapping.
- README / docs entries referencing the conclusion line — update if present.

## Risks & assumptions

- Wording for the 12 non-example skills is an operator-approved draft (Q1=A) and remains reviewable during implementation/review; the four named lines (plan/intake/implement/audit) are fixed by the item.
- An unmapped/future skill silently receiving "Ready to ship" is mitigated by AC1's explicit fallback and by documenting the mapping in `skill/report/SKILL.md` so new skills know to extend it.
- Scope creep risk: the change is confined to the Conclusion verdict lines; header, AC table, Meta-Data and producer-actions rendering are out of scope (see Constraints) — any further report-polish ideas should be filed as separate work items.
- Assumption: "Ready to ship" wording for audit is unchanged (per item description and related item SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI), so the two items do not conflict.

## Related work

- SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI — Audit report Conclusion can claim 'Ready to ship' when the audit failed (open, high). Partial overlap on the same Conclusion section: that item gates the audit skill's "Ready to ship" on the persisted audit verdict; this item changes wording per skill. Independent changes; audit's success line stays "Ready to ship" so no text conflict. Reference as related work, not a duplicate.
- SA-0MVYEZ3V3004AQXN — Clearer audit results (completed): colour/readability foundation this builds on (colour capability preserved as a constraint).
- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S / SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L — report helper skill creation + tests (completed): origin of the renderer being changed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which skills get skill-specific summary lines?" — Answer (operator): "A — all ~16 skills that call `render_report.py`, each with its own line." Source: interactive reply. Research: grep of `--skill-name` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows 16 callers (agent-log-review, audit, author-command, cleanup, code-review, effort-and-risk, find-related, implement, intake, machine-hygiene, plan, refactor, resolve-pr-comments, ship, test, triage); `report` skill itself renders no report (0 call sites). Mapping drafted in Desired change for operator confirmation.
- Q2: "Should the failure line become skill-specific too?" — Answer (operator): "A — yes, mirror the success line per skill." Source: interactive reply. Failure lines drafted as "Not <success>" / "<skill> incomplete" variants above; accepted pattern to confirm at review.

# `implement.py start` must not fork a worktree from a local parent branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`

Mirror of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MWFF40700014EE2** (`discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`).
Per the precedent producer decision for **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 ← AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(2026-09-25: "the fix and regression tests live in the SorraAgents counterpart; no
implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix lives here, where
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is.

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`, but
`_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is diverged or cannot
be fetched non-checked-out (`reason: "diverged_or_checked_out"`), and `phase_start` then
forks the worktree from that stale local `dev` anyway (`git_worktree_add(branch,
abs_wt_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <wt> dev`). The child
session inherits a base missing commits already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev` (`e38797b8` local-only,
  duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an unrelated
  `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against pre-fix source and went **red** on a failure
  `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS` still listing the deleted
  `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (`8d1c1aca`) by hand before it could pass its
  gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push to dev
initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and retried"), so this is
recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref whose commits are all contained in
`origin/<parent>` (a fast-forward ancestor of `origin/<parent>`), so a driven child never
starts behind the published base.

## Approach (decided)

The AI_Hell report listed two candidate approaches ("fork from `origin/<parent>`" or
"warn loudly"); the acceptance criteria pin the first and make the second mandatory
reporting, so both are in scope:

1. `_sync_parent_branch` reports `ahead`/`behind` counts (via
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) on every
   skip reason where the counts are computable, in addition to `reason`/`warning`.
2. A new resolver decides the fork base: **fork from
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` whenever the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, which includes the diverged case); otherwise keep the current local-branch
   base.** The local ref is never force-updated — a diverged local `dev` stays exactly as it
   is for the operator to reconcile.
3. `phase_start` records the choice: `report["steps"]["worktree_base"] = {ref, reason,
   ahead, behind}` and an extended "Implementation started"/"resumed" comment naming the base
   ref and, when the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
4. Fail-open is preserved: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch, or a dirty main checkout
   never blocks `start`; when the counts cannot be computed (fetch failed / no remote-tracking
   ref) the local branch remains the base exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded or the worktree is forked
  from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent branch
  was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first changed-scope
  gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh still fails
  open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch.

## Implementation sketch

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): add `ahead`/`behind` to the skipped results
    (`diverged`, `diverged_or_checked_out`, and the other safe-skip paths where computable).
  - New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
    returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`; picks
    `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when behind > 0.
  - `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): pass the resolved ref to `git_worktree_add`, record
    `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, and name it in the start/resume comment (~line 11431).
  - `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): document that the base may be a fully-qualified
    remote-tracking ref; assert the new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` (the
    `--track` upstream must not change — `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`).
- Tests (test-first, new file `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, following
  the hermetic-fixture patterns in `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` /
  `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (start section ~2204-2216, ~4029) and
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~357) — document the base-ref resolution and the new report
  keys/skip reasons.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2` (AI_Hell discovery report; counterpart of this item)
- SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 (completed) — `finish` now fast-forwards local `dev` after the push;
  that closes the *common* stale-local-dev case, leaving the diverged/lock-held skip this
  item fixes.
- SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO — main-checkout lock shared by `start`'s refresh and `finish`.
- SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF — `start` resume-from-worktree path resolved against the main checkout.
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree detection (same "stale base" family).

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a rebase and a red
gate on work someone else already shipped.
