# Fork the `start` worktree from `origin/<parent>` when the local parent is behind

Implement the fix specified by the parent item **SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK**, in TDD order,
on top of the harness delivered by **SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK**.

## Change

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

1. `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): on every safe-skip path where the counts are
   computable, add `ahead` / `behind` (from
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) to the
   result alongside `reason` / `warning`. Counts are best-effort: a failed `rev-list`
   leaves them absent and never fails the refresh.
2. New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
   returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`. It selects
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, covering diverged), otherwise the local `parent_branch`. It never
   updates the local ref and never force-moves anything.
3. `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): fork with the resolved ref instead of the bare
   local branch name, and record `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`.
4. `phase_start` start/resume comment (~line 11431): name the base ref used and, when
   the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
5. `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): accept/document a fully-qualified remote-tracking
   base ref, and keep the `--track` upstream behaviour (`branch.<new>.remote = origin`,
   `merge = refs/heads/<parent>`) so `finish`'s push-to-`dev` semantics are unchanged.

Preserve fail-open: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch or a dirty main checkout
must never block `start`, and a diverged local branch must never be force-updated.

## Tests (written first, inside this worktree)

Add to `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, using the fixture from
SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK. Write each case, observe it fail, record the red evidence in a
work-item comment, then implement until all pass. Tests and fix land together — never
commit a red tree (the `finish` changed-scope gate requires a passing suite).

New cases:

1. **Diverged local `dev`** (`ahead >0, behind >0`): `start` forks from
   `refs/remotes/origin/dev`; the new branch's merge-base with `origin/dev` is
   `origin/dev`'s tip; `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]` carries `ref`, `reason`,
   `ahead`, `behind`.
2. **Behind-only local `dev` with a skipped refresh** (lock held; and separately a dirty
   main checkout): still forks from `origin/dev` and `start` succeeds.
3. **Local-ahead-only `dev`** (`behind 0`): base stays the local `dev` branch.
4. **Fetch failed**: base stays the local `dev` branch, `start` succeeds, reason recorded.
5. **AC3 end-to-end**: a synthetic diverged branch where `origin/dev` carries a fix the
   stale local `dev` lacks; after `start` the new worktree's tree contains that fix, so a
   first changed-scope gate runs against the fixed source with no manual rebase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: when the local `dev` is diverged or behind, the worktree is
  forked from `refs/remotes/origin/dev` instead of the stale local ref, and the created
  branch's merge-base with `origin/dev` is `origin/dev`'s tip.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent
  branch was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind
  counts — `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]` carries `ref`, `reason`, `ahead`, `behind`,
  and the worklog start/resume comment states the same.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first
  changed-scope gate without a manual rebase: the regression test with a synthetic diverged
  local branch shows the new worktree's tree already contains the fix `origin/dev` carries.
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held, dirty-checkout or fetch-failed
  refresh still fails open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch
  (the diverged local `dev` tip is unchanged after `start`).
- **AC5** — The new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` in both base-ref paths, so
  `finish`'s push-to-`dev` path is unchanged.
- **AC6** — Red-first evidence for the new cases is recorded as a comment on this item
  before the implementation is committed, and no test is left skipped or xfail.
- **AC7** — `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` and the rest of the
  `skill/implement` changed scope pass via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`

## Impact

Child sessions start from the published base instead of a stale local `dev`, so a driven
child no longer needs a manual rebase before its first gate.

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item
  (SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR).
- Q: "Is trimming the per-project full test suite runtime in scope?" — Answer (operator,
  2026-11-13): "No — per-project (AI_Hell) suite trimming, sharding and
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` changes are out of scope for this epic." Source: same comment.
- Q: "What is the evidence base for the problem statement?" — Answer: the 2026-11-13
  AI_Hell analysis of 36 implement-skill sessions (668 min summed over a 388 min span;
  1.7x effective parallelism; 46 lock-waits, median 5 min, max 21.5 min; 21 rebases;
  9 no-op sessions). Source: comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR and the "Evidence" section
  above.
- Q: "Does the epic already own a measurement/verification item?" — Answer (this intake,
  research: `wl list --parent SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1`): no — the four original children all
  change code, so the outcome ACs had no owner; child 5
  (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) was created to own them.

### Plan session (2026-11-13)

- Q: "Are further clarifying questions needed before the decomposition is final?"
  Answer (agent, research: full re-read of all five children plus repository verification
  of `implement.py` Step 3c / `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `.githooks/pre-push`,
  `run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache and `phase_drive`): no — the four intake answers
  (concurrency target 6; per-project suite trimming out of scope; evidence base;
  measurement ownership) already fix scope, and every child's factual claims check out
  against the current code.
- Q: "Does each root cause need a separate test-only work item before implementation?"
  Answer (agent, applying the plan skill's vertical-slice rule): no — every child carries
  its own test acceptance criteria and names its test home in `**Key Files:**`, so each is
  a vertical slice (code + tests + docs) rather than a horizontal layer.
- Q: "Do the two lock-window children need sequencing?"
  Answer (agent): yes — the bounded-wait default (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) changes the same
  `phase_finish` lock-acquisition path that SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4 shrinks; installing a
  positive bound before the suite leaves the lock would introduce long (bounded) waits
  around a still-locked full suite. Dependency edge added:
  SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF depends on SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4.
- Review note (no decision needed): `.githooks/pre-push` is flagged by
  `validate_key_files_format()` only because hook scripts carry no file extension; the
  path is correct and was deliberately left unchanged.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **SA-0MPVO6JNI006ESN0** – Triage dev-full-suite failures (run 26780355787) (completed)

# Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast). When the lock is held, the
agent must re-enter the queue itself, so the skill guidance teaches a hand-rolled
`for attempt in 1..8; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder> ...`
loop. In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis this pattern produced the single worst tool
call — **45 minutes** absorbing five consecutive lock holders — and accounted for a
large share of the 37% `wait_for_job` time plus 48 min (7%) of separate `sleep`/`grep`
polling loops. Each fail-fast refusal is also a wasted model round-trip.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch: wants predictable, minimal waiting per session.
- **Implement-skill session** that currently has to script retry loops around
  `implement.py finish`.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session, I want one `finish` call to wait internally on the
  lock (bounded, with progress) so I do not burn model round-trips on retry loops.
- As an operator watching a batch, I want a waiting session to report who holds the
  lock and to fail with an actionable message only when the bound expires.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a waiting `finish` to perform **one** bounded internal wait on
the flock (with progress), instead of the agent scripting fail-fast retry loops around
it, so concurrent finishes do not multiply round-trips and confusing logs.

## Approach

- Make a positive bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the guidance default (or
  document setting it) so `finish` waits internally on the flock up to a generous
  bound, emitting progress.
- Remove the `for attempt in ... ; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job` retry-loop
  guidance from the implement skill; replace with the single bounded-wait instruction.
- Ensure the internal wait reports the holder and honours `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` cleanly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `implement.py finish` with a positive `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` waits on the
  lock internally within the bound, reporting the holder, and fails with an
  actionable message only when the bound expires.
- The implement skill docs contain no bespoke finish retry-loop pattern; they instruct
  a single bounded wait.
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A test covers: lock held → `finish` waits → holder releases → `finish` proceeds
  (no fail-fast refusal).
- Regression test that the wait is bounded (never hangs) and is signal-safe.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wait must stay bounded: a configured timeout always terminates the wait with an
  actionable refusal naming the holder and the lock path.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` must release the held lock and the child lock and exit cleanly
  (no orphaned locks).
- Default behaviour must stay safe for unattended sessions: a positive bound must not
  be able to wedge a batch indefinitely.
- Out of scope: changing the single-owner lock semantics or removing the lock.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.0` (fail fast), env `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  read by `_finish_lock_timeout()`; the bounded wait lives in
  `shared.repo_lock.RepoLock` via `acquire_main_checkout_lock`.
- The implement skill documents the current fail-fast behaviour, and sessions work
  around it with `for attempt ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder>` loops.
- Lock holders are recorded with pid/host metadata, so the holder can already be named
  in a refusal.

## Desired change

`finish` performs one bounded internal wait with progress and holder reporting; the
skill guidance describes that single call instead of a bespoke retry loop.

## Impact

An operator's concurrent batch stops multiplying model round-trips and multi-minute
tool calls on lock contention: a waiting session reports who holds the lock and
proceeds automatically once released.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `_finish_lock_timeout()`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock` call in `phase_finish`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — bounded wait implementation and holder reporting
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — guidance that must lose the bespoke retry-loop pattern
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py` — test homes for the wait behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — timeout documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper.
- implement test suite inherits IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT from the ambient environment and hangs for hours (SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB) — timeout inheritance hazard to keep in mind.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the other half of lock-wait reduction.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general-purpose lock queue service is out of scope;
  this item is one bounded wait inside `finish`.
- **Risk:** a long default bound could make an unattended batch appear hung; mitigation:
  progress output plus a clear expiry message, and the default chosen deliberately
  (documented) rather than "infinite".
- **Assumption:** the holder pid/identity metadata recorded by `RepoLock` is sufficient
  to name the holder in progress output.
- **Assumption:** removing the retry-loop guidance from the skill does not break driven
  sessions, which call `finish` once per child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: 2026-11-13 AI_Hell
36-session analysis on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment
SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), including the 45-minute worst-case tool call and the 48 min of
`sleep`/`grep` polling. Researched in the repository: `_finish_lock_timeout()` /
`DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and the bounded
wait in `skill/shared/repo_lock.py`.

# Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

Because concurrent finishes push to the shared `dev` ref, pushes frequently lose the
non-fast-forward race: in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis there were **21** rebase
events. Each rebase rewrites the commit onto a new base, producing a **new tree**, which
misses the tree-keyed gate cache and **re-runs the ~5.4-min full suite** inside the
lock. So a single work item can pay the full-suite cost repeatedly (e.g. AH-0MWEZZE5U,
AH-0MWEYVRUX and others showed 2–3 rebase rounds each).

## Users

- **Operator** running a concurrent fan-out batch into `dev`.
- **Implement-skill session** that loses the push race and today pays another full-suite
  run after rebasing.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session that lost the push race, I want to rebase and push
  without re-running the full suite, because my change content did not change.
- As an operator, I want the number of full-suite gate runs in a batch to stay close to
  the number of work items, not a multiple of it.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a rebased push not to re-run the full suite when the change
content is unchanged, so a lost push race costs seconds, not another 5 minutes.

## Approach (options to weigh)

- Serialise dev pushes (a short push queue / fast-forward retry that rebases only the
  ref, reusing the already-green tree verdict where the tree is provably identical).
- Or key the gate verdict on the **commit's change set / content hash** rather than the
  full tree, so a pure rebase (same diff, different base) reuses the verdict.
- Or batch dev advancement so a batch is rebased once.

## Acceptance criteria

- A push that loses the non-fast-forward race and is rebased onto a new base does
  **not** re-execute the full suite when the tree/diff is provably unchanged (cache
  hit demonstrated in a test).
- The safety property is preserved: a verdict is never reused for a tree/diff that
  actually differs.
- The number of full-suite gate runs for a concurrent fan-out drops measurably
  (recorded before/after).
- An automated test covers the rebase-then-push path reusing a prior green verdict, and
  a negative test proves a genuinely different tree/diff still misses the cache.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The gate must remain evidence about the **pushed** commit: a verdict may only be
  reused when the tested content is provably identical to what is pushed.
- No weakening of the release gate for `dev`/`main`; `scope=full` stays mandatory.
- Cannot rely on changing per-project suite runtime or sharding.
- Out of scope: redesigning the git transport retry policy for auth/transport failures.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  `dev`/`main` pushes and mirrors gate cache entries into the main checkout's
  `.worklog/cache`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` keys cached verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`
  and records `gate-subject` / `gate-verdict` provenance (`tree=`, cache hit/miss + age).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` raises a recoverable non-fast-forward error
  carrying a `rebase_cmd` hint, so the caller rebases onto `origin/dev` and retries —
  producing a new tree and therefore a cache miss today.

## Desired change

A rebased push of provably unchanged content reuses the existing green verdict, so a
lost push race no longer costs another full-suite run.

## Impact

Losing a push race in a concurrent batch costs seconds instead of another five-minute
full-suite run, so a batch's total gate time stops multiplying with the number of
rebases.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — tree-keyed verdict cache, `--gate-commit` binding, `gate-verdict` provenance
- `.githooks/pre-push` — gate invocation and cache mirroring for dev/main pushes
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `PUSH_FAILURE_NON_FAST_FORWARD`, the non-fast-forward exception and its `rebase_cmd` retry path
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` and `tests/test_test_cache.py` — gate cache/reuse tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — push retry / gate documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item extends.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the gate exists.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race handling prior art.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — both reduce gate cost under concurrency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (safety):** reusing a verdict for a different diff would let an untested change
  reach `dev`; mitigation: reuse only on provable content equality, with a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** batching dev advancement is a larger refactor; treat it as the
  fallback option, preferring the verdict-keying change.
- **Assumption:** a pure rebase produces an identical diff (so a change-set key would
  hit) even though the tree SHA differs.
- **Assumption:** the pre-push hook can be told the intended verdict key without
  weakening the "evidence about the pushed commit" property.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 21 rebase events and the
2–3-round repeats (AH-0MWEZZE5U, AH-0MWEYVRUX) in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the
parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the
repository: `.githooks/pre-push` gate invocation and cache mirroring,
`run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache, and the non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry path in
`implement.py`.

# Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis, **9 of 36** implement sessions were effectively
no-ops: 3 messages, ~50 s each — a driven child session that started, loaded the skill,
and exited without doing work (repeated for several child ids, e.g.
AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J, AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414).
Each is cheap individually but indicates the driver is re-spawning children whose work
is blocked or already done, wasting session startup and muddying the pipeline.

## Users

- **Operator** running `/skill:implement <parent>` drive chains: wants every spawned
  session to do real work.
- **Parent (epic) session** that spawns child sessions and must not waste fan-out slots.
- **Child session** that today starts only to discover there is nothing to do.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want the driver to skip children that are already terminal, blocked
  or held, so a batch spends its slots on real work.
- As a parent session, I want each spawned child session to be startable, so the drive
  report is a faithful record of work done.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the driver not to spawn a child session that will immediately
no-op, so fan-out slots and time are not spent on empty runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause identified for the no-op spawns (already-terminal child, blocked child, or
  an id collision).
- `phase_drive` does not spawn a session for a child that is terminal/blocked/held, with
  a test covering the observed pattern.
- Re-running the same batch produces zero no-op sessions.
- An automated test reproduces the observed no-op pattern (terminal/blocked/held child)
  and asserts no session is spawned, alongside a regression test that a genuinely
  startable child is still spawned.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Terminal children are never finished, reset or re-spawned (existing invariant).
- Blocked verdicts must never be overridden: a child held by a producer or an unmet
  dependency edge is a soft wait, not a work item to start.
- `max_child_sessions` / `finish_attempt_limit` bounds stay in force — the fix must not
  introduce unbounded retrying.
- Out of scope: reducing session start-up cost itself (skill loading), and the
  lock/gate performance work in the sibling items.

## Existing state

- `phase_drive` runs `parent` (subprocess-isolated) and spawns a fresh Pi session for
  `next_child`, re-fetching and classifying children via `_is_terminal_child` /
  `_reconcile_spawn_failure` after a failed spawn.
- The blocked verdict already stops the chain **without** spawning (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT),
  so the observed no-ops point at a gap between "what `parent` reported as next" and the
  child's actual state at spawn time (terminal/blocked/held/collision).

## Desired change

Before spawning, `phase_drive` re-validates that the reported `next_child` is genuinely
startable (non-terminal, not blocked, not held) and records the reason instead of
spawning when it is not.

## Impact

Operators stop paying session start-up and pipeline noise for children that do no work,
and a drive report reflects only real sessions — so a fan-out batch's wall-clock is not
padded by empty runs.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` spawn decision, `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `_is_terminal_child`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` and `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — drive-mode tests (spawn/no-spawn assertions, child locks)
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — drive recovery regression coverage
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — drive-phase documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- implement drive: run each epic child in an interactive Herdr pane (same tab) (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40) — pane spawning path.
- Failing finish bound / terminal reconciliation prior art (SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL, SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV) referenced in `phase_drive`'s contract.
- Blocked-verdict soft wait (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT) — the "do not spawn when blocked" precedent this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making spawn decisions optimistic-but-retried would hide the
  real defect; the fix must record *why* a child was skipped.
- **Risk:** a stale `parent` report could cause the driver to skip a genuinely startable
  child, stalling the chain; mitigation: re-fetch the child immediately before the spawn
  decision and keep the existing bounded re-run of `parent`.
- **Assumption:** the no-op sessions were driven by stale/incomplete child state rather
  than by a Pi session-start failure; the root-cause AC must confirm this before fixing.
- **Assumption:** the analysis sample (9 sessions, 3 messages each) is representative of
  driven-child no-ops.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 9 no-op sessions (~50 s,
3 messages) across AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J and
AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414, from the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the repository:
`phase_drive` and its spawn/reconcile helpers in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.

> **OPEN QUESTION (root cause):** the analysis recorded the symptom, not the mechanism.
> The implementing session must identify which of (already-terminal child, blocked child,
> id collision, spawn-time state change) caused the observed no-ops before changing
> behaviour — the AC makes this an explicit deliverable rather than an assumption.
data.title: Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up

# Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

The parent epic's outcome is stated as a measurable property: under a 6-way concurrent
`finish` fan-out no session should spend the majority of its wall-clock blocked on the
per-repository lock. Today's baseline (2026-11-13, 36 AI_Hell implement sessions) shows
the opposite — 1.7x effective parallelism, 37% of time in `wait_for_job`, 46 lock-waits
averaging 4.3 min (max 21.5 min). Nothing in the epic's child items produces that final
before/after evidence, so without this item the epic can be declared "done" while the
operator-visible symptom is unverified.

## Users

- **Operator** who decides whether a batch is fast enough and whether a fan-out of 6 is
  safe to run by default.
- **Producer** reviewing the epic: needs recorded evidence, not a claim, that the fix
  worked.
- **Future framework work** relying on the same session-analysis methodology.

User stories:

- As the operator, I want a recorded before/after comparison of the same session
  analysis so I can see whether a 6-way fan-out now finishes in roughly the time of one
  work item.
- As the producer, I want the epic's outcome ACs checked against real session logs
  before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want the epic's
lock-contention targets measured against real session logs and recorded, so the speed-up
is verified rather than assumed.

## Approach

- Re-run the 36-session style analysis (per-session `bash`-wait buckets, lock-wait
  medians/maxima, rebase count, full-suite gate run count) on sessions after the sibling
  fixes land.
- Reuse or extend the session-time analysis capability (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) rather than
  hand-rolling a new analyser.
- Compare against the 2026-11-13 baseline recorded on the parent epic and publish both
  numbers side by side.
- Exercise a genuine 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out if sessions alone do not reach
  concurrency 6.

## Acceptance criteria

- Measure a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out and record that no session spends the majority of its wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- Record a concrete before/after measurement using the same 36-session style analysis.
- The before/after numbers are posted on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1) and state
  explicitly which sibling items were in effect for the "after" run.
- If the targets are not met, the shortfall is recorded as findings with follow-up work
  items rather than reported as success.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Blocked by all four implementation children of the epic: measuring earlier would not
  reflect the fixes.
- Analysis must reuse the same bucketing definitions as the 2026-11-13 baseline so the
  comparison is apples to apples.
- Session logs are operator data: record aggregate metrics and session ids only, no
  prompt/response content.
- Out of scope: per-project suite runtime trimming, and changing changed-scope test
  selection.

## Existing state

- The 2026-11-13 baseline is recorded on the parent epic (analysis comment) with the
  exact metric definitions: summed session time vs wall-clock span, `bash`-wait share,
  `wait_for_job` bucket, lock refusal/wait counts, rebase events, full-suite gate runs.
- Session logs live under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` (e.g.
  `--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`); the analysis was ad hoc.
- A session-time analysis skill is tracked separately (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM).

## Desired change

The epic's lock-contention target is evidenced by a repeatable, recorded before/after
analysis, and any shortfall becomes visible follow-up work instead of an assumption.

## Impact

The operator can see, in recorded numbers, whether a 6-way fan-out now completes in
roughly the time of one work item — instead of trusting that the fixes helped.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish/lock reporting fields consumed by the analysis (`main_checkout_lock` report step, lock-wait metrics)
- `.githooks/pre-push` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — gate-run provenance (`gate-subject` / `gate-verdict`) used to count full-suite runs
- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — existing read-only session-log wait analyser (slot-wait re-measurement, SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) to reuse/extend rather than duplicate; session logs themselves live outside the repository under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — where the measurement method should be documented

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1) — carries the baseline metrics and the target.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — the analyser this item should reuse/feed.
- Siblings this measurement verifies: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4); Finish wait ergonomics (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC); Eliminate no-op drive retries (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R).
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent for a measurement-only follow-up item.
- Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S) — prior session-time analysis methodology.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** measuring before all siblings land produces a misleading "no improvement"
  verdict — mitigated by the explicit blocked-by edges and by naming which items were in
  effect.
- **Risk (scope creep):** turning this into a general performance dashboard is out of
  scope; it is a one-off verification with a reusable analyser where one already exists.
- **Risk:** ambient machine load skews wall-clock comparisons; mitigation: report the
  bucketed metrics (lock-wait counts/medians, gate-run counts), not just totals.
- **Assumption:** comparable session logs (similar work-item sizes) are available for the
  "after" run; if not, a synthetic 6-way fan-out provides the measurement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. Evidence: the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session
analysis and the operator decisions recorded on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1,
comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR) — concurrency target up to 6, per-project suite trimming
out of scope. Researched in the repository: the `main_checkout_lock` report step in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, gate provenance in `.githooks/pre-push` /
`run_tests.py`, and the session-log layout under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
data.title: Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis

# Set assignee per skill

## Problem statement

Skills currently claim work items using the producer identity (`Map`) as the assignee. This makes an agent's claim indistinguishable from a producer hold and prevents the claim reaper from identifying which skill is actually working. Each skill should instead claim with its own name.

## Users

- **Producers** — need to identify which skill is actively working on a work item from the assignee field.
- **Automated systems** (downtime dispatcher, claim reaper) — need accurate assignee attribution to detect and release stale claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Intake skill** — `intake.py start` defaults to `assignee="Intake"` when no explicit assignee is passed; callers that hard-code `--assignee Map` are updated to either omit the flag (using the new default) or use `--assignee Intake`.
2. **Plan skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim in the plan skill's documentation is updated to `--assignee Plan` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
3. **Implement skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Implement` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
4. **Audit skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Audit` (or removed if already using `--assignee ""`).
5. **All other skill documentation** — any remaining references to `--assignee Map` in SKILL.md files are updated to use the appropriate skill name.
6. **Assignee release unchanged** — the assignee-clearing behaviour on every terminal outcome (finish, auto-complete, abort, error) is preserved exactly as-is.

## Impact

Producers and automated systems can now distinguish which skill is actively working on a work item by inspecting the assignee field, and the claim reaper can reliably identify and release stale skill-level claims.

## Constraints

- Only the *claim* assignee changes; release-by-default on every terminal outcome is unaffected.
- The `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT` constant and the `claim_release.py` shared module must continue to treat `Map` as a claimable identity — no changes to shared infrastructure.
- No new work items should be created during the change; only existing skill documentation and any skill scripts that hard-code `Map` are modified.

## Existing state

- The intake skill instructs agents to pass `--assignee Map` to `intake.py start`.
- The `claim_release.py` module defines `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"` and treats it as a normal claim (released on terminal outcomes).
- The plan skill already claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).
- The implement skill also claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).

## Desired change

Replace `--assignee Map` with the skill's own name (e.g., `--assignee Intake`, `--assignee Audit`) in skill documentation and any scripts that hard-code this pattern, so each skill's claim is self-attributing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — Update `--assignee Map` references to `--assignee Intake`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/scripts/intake.py` — Change default assignee in `cmd_start` from None to `"Intake"`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md` — Check for any `--assignee Map` references; update if present.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/claim_release.py` — No changes required (Map remains a valid claimable identity).

## Related work

- SA-0MW7QTAHW0030FGV — Planned items are still left with an assignee (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK — T1: Table-driven assignee-release regression matrix (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL — Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ — Migrate callers and pin intentional holds (completed)
- SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM — implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the task scope is clear from the work-item description.

## Context

Child of **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU** (Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects). Implements parent **AC4** (dated, idempotent scheduled output) and **AC5** (failures surfaced, never a silent success). Producer decisions Q1–Q3 are settled in the parent brief: per-project `/skill:test-churn` entries, checked-in managed-root list, 7-day default interval.

## Scope

A thin, deterministic wrapper over the existing analyser
(`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`) that a scheduled
`/skill:test-churn` run invokes, so a scheduled run cannot drift from the
documented output contract. The wrapper owns path resolution and exit-code
propagation only — all analysis stays in the analyser (no duplicate logic).

Design decisions (documented, not open questions):

- Output is pinned to `<root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md`
  and `test_churn_data.json`; `--report-name`/`--json-name` are not exposed by
  the wrapper so the scheduled contract cannot be re-pointed per call.
- **History is intentionally unbounded** by default (`--max-commits 0`). The
  analyser's growth metrics are whole-history by definition, so a default
  commit bound would silently change the trend. CPU cost is mitigated by the
  staggering and `priority: low` in the provisioning child, per the parent's
  CPU-blocking risk. `--since`/`--max-commits` remain pass-through options for
  constrained runs.
- `--date` is injectable so tests are clock-independent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run_scheduled.py --root <git repo> --date 2026-11-14` writes exactly
  `reports/test-churn/2026-11-14/test_churn_report.md` and
  `reports/test-churn/2026-11-14/test_churn_data.json` beneath the root and
  exits 0.
- Re-running the identical command on the same date overwrites those two
  files, and the recursive file/directory listing of `reports/test-churn/` is
  byte-for-byte identical before and after (no numbered duplicates, no nested
  dated directories).
- A root that is absent, is not a git work tree, or fails inside the analyser
  (`GitError`) yields a non-zero exit code and a per-root error line on
  stderr, plus a run summary; it is never reported as success.
- `--since`, `--max-commits`, `--branch` and `--quiet` are passed through to
  the analyser unchanged (covered by a test that asserts the child-process
  argv).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Scheduled runs" section covering
  enable/disable, the dated output path, failure behaviour (non-zero exit,
  stderr), the interval override, and the whole-history rationale.
- Tests exercise each bullet above and are run through `/skill:test`.

### Parent AC traceability (verbatim parent ACs delivered by this slice)

- Parent AC4: Each scheduled run writes `<project-root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and `test_churn_data.json`; a re-run on the same date deterministically overwrites those two files and creates no duplicate files or directories.

## Context

Child of **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU**. Implements parent **AC1** (schema-valid entry), **AC2** (create-if-absent provisioning, including Tableau-Card-Engine which has no scheduled-prompts file), **AC3** (mandatory deterministic staggering — no CPU blocking), **AC6** (configurable interval, default 7 days) and the provisioning/staggering half of **AC7**.

The schedule file format is owned by the external `worklog`/herdr package
(`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`): `entries[]` of
`{id, prompt, intervalDays, lastTriggeredAt, time?, priority?}`; an absent file
is an empty set, a malformed file is an empty set (logged), and an invalid
entry is skipped. Provisioning must never rewrite or drop entries it does not
own.

## Scope

`skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py` — create-if-absent
insertion of one `/skill:test-churn` entry per managed root, with deterministic
staggering.

Documented scheme (implemented and tested here, documented in AC8 files):

- **Window:** local `02:00` + **30-minute** steps (`02:00, 02:30, …`), so eight
  roots occupy `02:00–05:30`. This deliberately avoids the `/skill:standup`
  slot at `06:05`; the parent brief's "e.g. 02:00 + 40-minute steps" is
  illustrative and a 40-minute step would put the 7th/8th slot at `06:00`/`06:40`,
  contradicting the binding "away from 06:05" constraint.
- **Day staggering:** `lastTriggeredAt = now − (index % intervalDays) days`, so
  the eight roots fall due on spread days across the 7-day cycle (the 8th root
  shares index 0's day but has a unique `time`, so no two roots are ever due in
  the same idle cycle).
- **Priority:** `priority: "low"` on the new entry, so a whole-history scan
  yields to the project's maintenance routines (schema default is `high`).
- **Idempotence:** never re-stagger or rewrite an existing
  `/skill:test-churn` entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For each managed root, provisioning inserts
  `{"id": "/skill:test-churn", "prompt": "/skill:test-churn", "intervalDays": 7,
  "time": "HH:MM", "priority": "low", "lastTriggeredAt": "<ISO-8601>"}` into
  `<root>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, creating `.worklog/` and the file
  when absent (the Tableau-Card-Engine case).
- All pre-existing entries — including their `lastTriggeredAt`, `time`,
  `priority`, unknown extra keys and schema-invalid entries — survive unchanged
  and in order, with the new entry appended; an unparseable (malformed) file is
  left untouched and reported as an error with a non-zero exit code.
- A second run reports "already present" for every root and writes nothing
  (assert unchanged bytes and mtimes); an existing entry is never re-staggered.
- Staggering is deterministic for a given `--now` and root list: every root has
  a unique `time` inside the documented window, `06:05` is never used, and the
  `lastTriggeredAt` day offsets are spread as `index % intervalDays`.
- `--dry-run` reports planned writes and performs none; `--root` (repeatable)
  overrides the checked-in list; `--interval-days` overrides the default 7 in
  both the entry and the day-offset arithmetic.
- Tests cover every bullet above (insert, preserve, idempotent re-run,
  create-if-absent, malformed config, unique times, spread offsets, dry-run,
  flags), run through `/skill:test`.

### Parent AC traceability (verbatim parent ACs delivered by this slice)

- Parent AC1: A `/skill:test-churn` entry is registered in SorraAgents' `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` using the existing schema (`id`, non-empty `prompt`, positive `intervalDays`, valid `HH:MM` `time`, and `lastTriggeredAt`), with the first provision setting a deterministic, staggered `lastTriggeredAt` seed and a distinct `time` (see AC3); re-running provisioning neither duplicates the entry, re-staggers it, nor changes any other entry's `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Parent AC3: **Staggering (no CPU blocking):** provisioned entries are spread deterministically across the managed set so no two projects are due in the same idle cycle. Each entry gets a unique `time` within a documented window (away from the 06:05 standup slot), and its `lastTriggeredAt` seed offsets its `intervalDays` cycle by a project-index-derived amount. The scheme is deterministic for a given managed-root list and clock (injectable `--now` for tests), documented, and covered by tests asserting no duplicate `time` values and evenly spread day offsets.
- Parent AC6: The interval is configurable per entry in `scheduled-prompts.json` and via a provisioning `--interval-days` flag; the default (**7 days, weekly**) is documented in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` with its rationale.
- Parent AC7: Automated tests cover: entry provisioning (insert, preserve other entries, idempotent re-run, create-if-absent including an absent file, malformed or invalid config), staggering (unique `time`, spread day offsets, no re-stagger on re-run), managed-root iteration (existing, absent and non-git roots), date-partitioned output and idempotent overwrite, and non-zero failure propagation.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py (new)
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_scheduled_runs.py
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md

## Out of scope

- Executing the provisioning against sibling project roots (next child item).
- Any change to the external herdr/worklog package.

## Impact

Every managed project becomes self-registering for weekly test-health evidence, spread across the week so no two heavy scans start together.

# Race-clobber restore regression tests

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B (audit restore lost-update). Test-first slice: land
the regression suite for the concurrent-`wl sync` clobber **before** the fixes
(F2/F3), so each fix is proven by a red-then-green test.

## Scope

Deterministic clobber injection for the audit lifecycle restore paths: an
injectable `wl` runner/store that reverts an item to a stale
`open`/`plan_complete` snapshot at a scripted point (before the next `wl show`
readback, or after a verified readback), modelling the concurrent `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ class).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` after the first verified restore readback and asserts the settle re-verification restores the item again.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore, even when the clobber lands on the first restore write.
- [ ] A regression test raises an exception after the `in_progress` claim (audit lease / checkpoint store) and asserts the captured pre-audit state is restored, never `in_progress`.
- [ ] A JS unit test drives `checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` with a clobbered restore, asserts one bounded retry, and asserts the state file is retained when the restore cannot be verified.
- [ ] The harness (injectable runner recording every `wl update`/`wl show`, with scripted clobber points (a) before the first readback and (b) after a verified readback) lives in `skill/audit/tests/`; the suite is red pre-fix (red run recorded in a work-item comment) and green after the fixes; no duplication of existing `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` coverage.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_restore_race.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`

## Out of scope

Fixing the restore paths (children F2/F3); fixing the general `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ).

# Verified-retry in-run lifecycle restore

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B. Python runner half of the race-safe restore.

## Scope

Make every in-run restore path converge under a concurrent `wl sync`: bounded
settle-verify-retry, the `in_progress` claim inside the `try/finally` guard,
and no side-effect-demotion window after the audit is persisted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore: `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` re-reads the persisted lifecycle after a bounded settle interval and re-applies the identical terminal write once, keeping the loud diagnostic and non-zero exit when it cannot converge.
- [ ] `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` uses the same bounded verify-then-retry (today it writes once and reads once) and reports non-zero when the restore is unverified.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path via `try/finally`, including exceptions raised after the `in_progress` claim: the claim moves inside `cmd_issue`'s guarded region so audit-lease acquisition, checkpoint-store open or an interrupt still restores the captured pre-audit state exactly once.
- [ ] An explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict still demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` deliberately and verified, while an infra-fallback-tainted `No` or a cascade-suppressed demotion restores the captured pre-audit state instead - after the persist step, the restore is re-asserted and verified immediately, closing the `wl audit-set` reversion window without clobbering `auditedAt`/`auditResult`.
- [ ] Restore writes reuse the shared `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` claim/assignee semantics (the claim-release predicate, not a re-derived copy, so `--assignee ""` and the assignee-release invariant hold), use the existing `ctx.worklog_dir` resolution (cwd-independent), and use CAS flags (`--if-status` / `--if-stage`) where they avoid a redundant write.
- [ ] The happy-path `Ready to close: Yes` advance makes no extra `wl show` calls; the added reads on restore paths are documented in a work-item comment, with no measurable audit-duration regression.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` or `in_progress` as a side effect of any audit path, and an unverified restore is never reported as success (loud diagnostic, non-zero exit).
- [ ] The F1 race suite and the existing `skill/audit/tests/` suite are green.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_restore_race.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`

## Constraints

Core auditing semantics (what is audited, how verdicts are calculated) must not
change; only the lifecycle-restore path.

## Impact

Audits that hit a concurrent `wl sync` can no longer park a work item in the wrong lifecycle or silently overwrite another session's update, so a release candidate is never knocked out of `in_review` by the audit that was supposed to check it.

# Verified-retry parent-side abort restore

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B. JS half of the race-safe restore: the
SIGKILL/abort state-file recovery used by the release gate.

## Scope

`check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` logs
`Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`, then issues a bare
`wl update`, deletes the state file unconditionally and never verifies the
result - the exact lost-update path quoted in the parent item. Make it
converge and never silently lose the restore.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` verifies the restore with a `wl show <id> --json` readback through an injectable boundary, retries the identical restore command once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered it, and reports an unverified restore loudly (naming the item and the manual recovery command) instead of logging success.
- [ ] An unverified restore leaves the `.audit_state_<id>.json` file in place so a later gate run retries (bounded per run, idempotent across runs); the file is deleted only after a verified restore.
- [ ] Every consumer of the abort state file (`check-audit-gate.js`, plus `refresh-audits.js` / `run-release.js` where they restore directly) routes through the single verified helper - no bare `wl update` restore copy remains, asserted by a test that scans the ship scripts.
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` cover a verified restore removing the file, a clobbered restore retried once then succeeding, an unverified restore keeping the file and warning, and unchanged corrupt/absent state-file behaviour.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` and the audit test suite are green.

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js`
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`

# Verdict-demotion policy documented and pinned

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B. Implements plan decision D1 (parent AC1) once the
producer confirms or overrules producer question Q3 recorded in the parent
Appendix. **Do not start this item before Q3 is answered.**

## Scope

Document and pin the reconciled contract: a genuine explicit
`Ready to close: No` demotes deliberately (and verifiably); no other audit path
may demote. Documentation and contract tests only - no behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/audit/SKILL.md` "Status Lifecycle" documents that an explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` deliberately and verified (audit-reject workflow), while an infra-fallback-tainted, aborted, timed-out or crashed audit never demotes, with both outcomes readback-verified under bounded retry.
- [ ] `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` gains a short "Race-safe lifecycle restore" section describing the settle-verify-retry contract, the abort state-file handshake (written before the claim, deleted only after a verified restore) and the bounded retry budget.
- [ ] Tests pin the contract without duplicating existing coverage: an explicit `No` demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` (verified); a fallback-tainted `No` restores the captured pre-audit state; the F1 race suite owns the concurrent-`wl sync` clobber dimension.
- [ ] The parent's AC1 wording and plan decision D1 are reconciled with the producer's answer to Q3 and recorded in the parent Appendix.
- [ ] Docs use UK English and every command shown runs as written.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`

## Impact

Auditors and producers can point at one written policy for what a failing verdict does to a work item — reject it back to the queue, or leave it where it is — instead of inferring it from the audit runner's code.

# Agent Skill Linter

**Headline:** A new `skill-linter` skill that scans `SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` files in the tracked skills tree, removes duplicated content and non-essential work-item IDs / workflow-comment noise, and produces a permission-gated recommendation report for content removal and brevity rewrites — scheduled to run at least weekly.

## Problem statement

The `skill/*/SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` files in this repository are the canonical source of the deployed agent skills (via the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink), and they have grown organically: content is duplicated across files, work-item IDs and workflow-traceability prose accumulate inline, and verbose blocks survive past their usefulness. The earlier one-off refactor (SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT) trimmed these files manually, but nothing keeps them from regressing. Agents load these files on every session, so bloat directly costs context budget and directive clarity.

## Users

- **AI agents** running Pi sessions — they load `SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` as instructions; lean, deduplicated files mean less context consumed and clearer directives.
- **Human maintainers** editing skills — a linter report with full context around proposed deletions makes review fast and safe.
- **Operators** running the weekly maintenance schedule — the report tells them exactly what to approve.

### Example user stories

- **As an** agent operator, **I want** a weekly skill-linter run, **so that** skills stay concise and deduplicated without manual effort.
- **As a** maintainer, **I want** proposed removals and rewrites presented with full context, **so that** I can approve or reject each change with confidence.
- **As an** agent, **I want** SKILL.md files free of non-essential work-item IDs and workflow comments, **so that** my context window is spent on instructions, not traceability noise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic duplicate detection:** The linter identifies duplicated content within and across the `skill/*/SKILL.md` files (and the repo `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), reporting file paths, line spans, and the duplicated text for each instance.
- **AC2 — Automatic safe fixes:** Running with `--apply` removes exact-duplicate content and clearly non-essential work-item IDs / workflow-comment noise (heuristic rules documented in the skill reference); `--dry-run` (default for the scheduled run) reports exactly what would change with full context and changes nothing.
- **AC3 — Permission-gated recommendations:** Content that could be removed (but is not clearly safe) and content that could be rewritten for brevity without losing clarity are reported with full context (file, section, current text, proposed text, rationale) and are never modified automatically — applying them requires explicit operator approval.
- **AC4 — Weekly scheduling:** The skill ships a cron-install helper (e.g. `--install-cron weekly`) and documents the installed line; a weekly `--dry-run` report is produced on schedule.
- **AC5 — Test coverage and regression gate:** Unit tests cover duplicate detection, ID/comment stripping, and report formatting; a changed-scope test gate passes; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite:** The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Skill authors can run one command to keep all skills and agent instructions lean and deduplicated, with every proposed change reviewable before it is applied — no more manual hygiene sweeps or regressing bloat.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary:** the new skill lives in `skill/skill-linter/` (scripts, tests, SKILL.md) with a reference doc in `docs/dev/`; the context-budget gate (`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`) must not be exceeded by the new files.
- **Read-only by default:** the linter must never modify files unless explicitly run with `--apply` (or an approved recommendation is applied by the operator); the weekly run is `--dry-run`.
- **No LLM dependency for core detection:** duplicate/ID detection must be deterministic (regex + structural comparison); LLM assistance is optional for brevity *recommendations* and must never gate the deterministic core.
- **Follow existing skill conventions:** hyphenated skill name, SKILL.md in the skill dir, scripts under `scripts/`, tests under `tests/`, shared-library imports resolved via the global skills path only (no script copies).
- **No scope creep:** this item creates the linter skill and its report/apply machinery; it does not itself rewrite the existing skill files (that is follow-up work driven by the first weekly report).

## Existing state

- `skill/*/SKILL.md` — 23+ files, ~6,000 lines total; known duplication and inline work-item IDs (e.g. audit 68, ship 26, test 17, report 12, implement 9 occurrences of `SA-…` IDs).
- `AGENTS.md` (repo root + `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` at repo root) — loaded as global agent instructions.
- One-off refactor epic **SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT** (completed) already trimmed these files once; no automated regression guard exists today.
- Related tooling exists: `context-audit` skill measures context size of these files (regression gate), and `ste100-experiment` measured STE-style brevity — neither lints content quality.

## Desired change

Introduce `skill/skill-linter/` with a CLI (`lint_skills.py`, style consistent with sibling skills): scan → detect duplicates / non-essential IDs & workflow comments / removable content / rewrite candidates → emit a structured report (text or JSON) with full context per finding → `--apply` applies only the safe-fix classes → `--install-cron weekly` prints/installs a crontab line for the weekly dry-run report. The skill is invoked as `/skill:skill-linter` with the same script-resolution pattern as sibling skills (`$(skill_path skill-linter)/scripts/...`).

## Key Files:

- `skill/skill-linter/SKILL.md` — new skill definition (lint rules, invocation, permission flow).
- `skill/skill-linter/scripts/lint_skills.py` — deterministic scanner + report generator + `--apply`/`--dry-run`/`--install-cron`/`--json` flags.
- `skill/skill-linter/tests/test_lint_skills.py` — unit tests for duplicate detection, ID stripping, report formatting, dry-run immutability.
- `docs/dev/skill-linter-reference.md` — reference doc: rules, heuristics, exit codes, cron installation.
- `skill/*/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — lint targets (read-only unless `--apply`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **False-positive deletions** — a heuristic could flag content as duplicated/non-essential when it is meaningful; mitigated by `--dry-run` as the default, full context in every report entry, and `--apply` only touching the clearly-safe fix classes.
- **LLM-variance in brevity recommendations** — LLM-produced rewrite proposals may vary run to run; mitigated by keeping them recommendation-only (never auto-applied) and requiring operator approval.
- **Cron not actually installed** — the helper prints the cron line for the operator to install (mirrors `wiki_watch`); the skill must not claim the schedule is active until installed.
- **Context-budget regression** — the new SKILL.md + scripts add context; must fit the existing `context-budget.thresholds.json` gate or the gate is updated deliberately (follow-up, not this item).
- **Assumption: repo is the lint target** — linting `skill/` + repo-root `AGENTS.md`/`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` covers the deployed skills because `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to this repo's `skill/`.
- **Assumption: skill does not rewrite existing files in this item** — the first weekly report drives follow-up work; this item only builds the linter (scope-creep guard).

## Related work

- **SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT** (completed) — one-off epic "Refactor AGENTS.md, commands, and skill files for conciseness and to remove duplication"; this linter is the automated, repeatable successor.
- **SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G** (completed) — "SorraAgents AGENTS.md: reference global instead of duplicating 20KB"; the AGENTS.md de-duplication precedent the linter should enforce (find-related report, 2026-11-14).
- **SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W** (completed) — split global vs project AGENTS.md (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` canonical source + symlink install); relevant to the linter's AGENT/AGENTS.md scope.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** (completed) — "Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness"; sibling one-off conciseness refactor in the same spirit.
- **SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP / SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1** (completed) — startup-context measurement and context-budget gate (`measure_context.py`, `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`); linter must not regress these gates.
- **`skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`** — measures the same files; complementary (measures size, linter improves quality).
- **`skill/ste100-experiment/`** — STE-style brevity experiment; relevant evidence for the brevity-recommendation rule design.
- **`skill/author-command/SKILL.md`** — skill-authoring conventions to follow.

> Related-work report also inserted into the item description by `find_related` (IDs SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB, SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W, SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: Which SKILL.md/AGENTS.md files should the linter examine? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option A accepted — SorraAgents repo only** (`skill/` + repo-root AGENTS.md); the repo IS the canonical source of deployed skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills` symlinks to it), so repo-only scope covers the deployment. CLI accepts a `--target` path so broader scans are possible later. Source: interactive reply ("continue").
- Q2: Lint only AGENT.md, only AGENTS.md, or both variants? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option C accepted — both variants treated identically.** Source: interactive reply ("continue").
- Q3: Output format? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option A + description text — report-only by default**, applying only the explicitly-authorized safe-fix classes under `--apply` (per item description: duplicated content and non-essential IDs/comments are removed; removals and brevity rewrites are recommended and require permission). Source: interactive reply ("continue") + canonical description wording.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-14 (plan skill, session via herdr-downtime):** Decomposed into 6 child work items (test-first vertical slices); dependency edges wired; parent-AC traceability restatements added to each child; six automated review stages passed; AC coverage review reached `proceed` (100%); stage advanced to `plan_complete`. See comment SA-C0MWGB3SDL006T8UX.

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.

## Impact

The release workflow can now show the agent every pending release candidate with its impact in one read-only packet, so the patch/minor/major call reflects what actually changed for users instead of guesswork.
