# Investigate a lingering `implement` assignee left on a completed driven child

## Observation

Child `WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI` (ContextHub) was implemented by a driven session
(headless `pi -p "/skill:implement ..."`) spawned by `implement.py drive`. It
reached `completed` / `in_review` with commit `691cbecdc`, its terminal
transition and 'Implementation complete.' comment were written at
2026-11-25T23:54:17Z, and the driver removed its worktree and continued to the
next child.

That item's `updatedAt` later moved to 2026-11-26T00:21:54Z (about 27 min
after the terminal write) with **no accompanying comment**, and the item was
left carrying a non-empty `assignee` of `implement`. Its sibling children
(`WL-0MWJE9J2Y001VZ1M`, `WL-0MWJE9IEH001R3P1`, `WL-0MWJE9MIR005SBQK`) all ended
with an empty assignee, so the release worked for them.

A non-empty assignee is a scheduling hold, so the claim was cleared by hand
(`wl update WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI --assignee "" --if-assignee implement`); the
work itself was unaffected.

## Root cause — confirmed (2026-11-27)

The later writer was neither `implement.py` (`phase_finish` / `phase_drive` /
`phase_parent` / `_finalise_stranded_child`) nor the downtime dispatcher. It was
the **`wl sync` merge resolver** in the `wl` CLI
(`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/sync/field-merge.ts`,
`mergeDifferentTimestampItems()`).

Evidence — `ContextHub/.worklog/logs/sync.log.1`, sync round resolved at
2026-11-26T00:18:23Z (the observed `updatedAt` 00:21:54Z follows it):

```
Conflict item=WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI ... type=different-timestamp
  local=2026-11-25T23:54:18.399Z remote=2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z
  field=status   chosen=local  reason=local has completed status (close) local="completed" remote="in-progress" chosen="completed"
  field=sortIndex chosen=remote reason=remote is newer (2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z) local=600 remote=800 chosen=800
  field=assignee chosen=remote reason=remote is newer (2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z) local="" remote="implement" chosen="implement"
  field=stage    chosen=local  reason=local has done stage (close) local="in_review" remote="intake_complete" chosen="in_review"
```

The merge resolved the **close** in favour of the local side for `status` and
`stage`, but `assignee` fell through to the generic default-vs-value /
newest-wins rule, so the losing side's non-empty claim was resurrected onto an
item the *same merge* had just marked `completed` / `in_review`. A merge writes
no comment, which explains the comment-less `updatedAt` bump. The
`restoreSide` guard (WL-0MWMRNL2W003W5R3) covers only restore-versus-tombstone
pairs, so it does not apply here. The sibling children were unaffected because
their records were not in conflict in that round.

Not the merge field policy: WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ deliberately made `assignee` an
ordinary merge field so a cleared `""` propagates. The defect is
*intra-record incoherence* — a terminal status paired with the losing side's
live claim — not the field policy. WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF is the same class of
defect in the tombstone direction.

## Scope

- **Owning fix (cross-repo):** `src/sync/field-merge.ts` in the ContextHub repo
  (`wl` CLI). It cannot be built, tested or worktreed from this repository, so
  it is tracked as a cross-repo item (see the plan child below) rather than
  implemented here.
- **This repository:** a post-sync defensive backstop (a terminal item can never
  keep a claim), regression tests and documentation, per the assignee-release
  invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The merge-conflict root cause is recorded and cited by the cross-repo merge
      item.
- [ ] A terminal-claim repair releases an assignee on a completed item
      regardless of claim age, idempotently, with a comment naming the previous
      assignee.
- [ ] The terminal-claim repair never clears needsProducerReview, the only
      persistent hold.
- [ ] A regression test proves a completed item's claim is released and a
      non-terminal claim untouched.
- [ ] A test proves the post-sync hook runs the terminal-claim repair after a
      sync.
- [ ] docs/dev/assignee-release.md documents the merge-resurrection failure mode
      and the repair backstop.
- [ ] A ContextHub work item tracks the merge claim and close coherence fix with
      a failing-first TypeScript test.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee`, `release_claim`,
  `reap_stale_claims` (the TTL sweep that deliberately skips terminal items).
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — `sync_worklog()` / `_run_reaper`, the
  post-sync hook the backstop plugs into.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_claim_release.py` — claim-release unit tests.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worklog_sync.py` — post-sync reaper hook tests.
- `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` — the canonical backstop documentation.
- Cross-repo (ContextHub, not this checkout):
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/sync/field-merge.ts` and its sync
  merge test suite.

## Plan

Vertical slices, test-first:

1. **Test: post-sync backstop releases terminal-item claims** (task, tests) —
   failing-first coverage in `skill/shared/tests/`.
2. **Release terminal-item claims in the post-sync backstop** (task) — the
   `claim_release` helper plus the `worklog_sync` hook.
3. **Document the sync-merge claim resurrection backstop** (docs).
4. **Record the merge claim/close coherence defect in the ContextHub store**
   (task) — the cross-repo tracking item that owns the real fix.

Children 1 → 2 → 3 are dependency-ordered; child 4 is independent and may run
first because it hands the root cause to the owning repository.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which code path wrote `assignee: implement` onto a `completed` item ~27
  min after its terminal transition?" — Answer (agent, research): the `wl sync`
  merge resolver `mergeDifferentTimestampItems()`; close-preservation wins
  `status`/`stage` per field while `assignee` uses newest-wins, resurrecting the
  losing side's claim. Evidence:
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/logs/sync.log.1` lines
  13826–13831 (round resolved 2026-11-26T00:18:23Z).
- Q: "Does the fix belong in this repository?" — Answer (agent, research +
  documented assumption): no. `wl`'s source is the ContextHub repo; this
  checkout cannot build or worktree it (worktree isolation + repository
  boundary disciplines). Assumption: this repo supplies the defensible backstop
  (invariant enforcement) and a cross-repo item carries the owning fix. Cheap to
  reverse if the producer prefers a single-repo change.
- Q: "Should the backstop replace the TTL reaper?" — Answer (agent, research):
  no. The reaper is TTL-bounded, comment-recording and deliberately skips
  terminal items; the new repair targets terminal items only and reuses
  `should_release_assignee` / `release_claim`. Both are idempotent and
  complementary.
- Q: "Is a producer decision required before implementing the backstop?" —
  Answer (agent): no. The assignee-release invariant already requires a release
  on every terminal outcome; adding a terminal-item backstop enforces the
  documented rule and does not widen the hold model.

Plan: changelog — 2026-11-27: root cause confirmed from the ContextHub sync
conflict log; ACs 2 and 3 of the original description (implement-skill writer /
dispatcher writer) are answered negatively and rewritten into one backstop AC
plus a cross-repo tracking AC; plan children added.

## Impact

A finished work item stops carrying a phantom scheduling hold, so hold
reporting and dispatch decisions reflect reality instead of a stale claim.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX** — the epic whose drive surfaced this
  (`discovered-from`).
- **WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI** — the affected child; see its assignee-release
  comment.
- **WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ** — decided `assignee` is an ordinary merge field (the
  policy is preserved by this plan).
- **WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF** — the same merge-resurrection class in the tombstone
  direction.
- **WL-0MWMRNL2W003W5R3** — the `restoreSide` guard that covers only
  restore-versus-tombstone pairs.

## Problem statement

SKILL.md files are growing large — the 10 largest total ~312KB, with the audit SKILL.md alone at 83KB (504 lines). This increases per-session token consumption. There are clear opportunities to reduce size without losing functionality.

## Users

- **AI agents** that load SKILL.md files into their context window at session start.
- **Operators** who need to maintain and understand skill behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every SKILL.md file is reviewed and reduced in size; each child item produces a measurable reduction (target: ≥20% size reduction per item) without removing functional instructions.
2. Duplicated boilerplate (report rendering, tool-output budget, background job etiquette) is extracted to a single shared reference (`skill/shared/`) and each skill references it.
3. All non-essential work-item ID references (SA-0..., AH-0...) are removed from SKILL.md files; traceability is preserved via comments on the parent work item or in the git history, not in the skill docs.
4. Each child item's PR includes a summary report documenting: original size, new size, percentage reduction, sections removed or extracted, and evidence that no functional instruction was lost.
5. The skill-linter is updated to flag near-duplicate boilerplate in SKILL.md files as an automated finding.
6. After all children are implemented, the total SKILL.md token footprint is reduced by at least 25% compared to the pre-change baseline.

## Impact

AI agent sessions will consume fewer tokens loading skill instructions, reducing context-window pressure across the project.

## Constraints

- Functional instructions must not be removed — only consolidated, referenced externally, or stripped as non-essential traceability noise.
- All children must pass the build + test gate before dev push.
- Each removal must be accompanied by a report demonstrating no functional regression.
- Existing skill-linter tests must not be broken.

## Existing state

- 26 SKILL.md files total; 10 largest account for ~312KB.
- skill-linter already detects 278 near-duplicate sections and 9 exact duplicates across skills.
- Prior work: SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR (Reduce initial LLM context from skills), SA-0MRGV9NJJ00720K5 (Refactor large skill files for conciseness), SA-0MWJWJ1HV000EBKP (Roll out tool-output budget guidance). These reduced some files but size has grown again.
- 225 work-item ID references scattered across SKILL.md files (audit: 113, ship: 40, test: 25, implement: 14, report: 8, find-related: 8, refactor: 6, plan: 7).

# Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose

## Problem statement

SorraAgents skills recover a work item's acceptance criteria by regexing the
`## Acceptance Criteria` section out of the work item's `description` (canonical
implementation: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria`).
Worklog is adding a first-class `acceptance_criteria` table with one row per
criterion — stable id, ordering, text, status (`met|unmet|partial|modified`)
and, for `modified` rows, the original text plus the justification. Skills must
switch from prose parsing to the table so a criterion has identity and status.

## Users

- **Pi agent sessions** that run skills consuming acceptance criteria programmatically: `audit`, `implement`, `find-related`, `plan`, `intake`, `report`.
- **Developer** maintaining those skills — needs predictable, testable AC behaviour regardless of description edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every skill that extracts acceptance criteria programmatically reads them from
  the worklog table (`wl ac show <id> --json`) instead of parsing description
  text; `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` either
  delegates to the table or remains only as an explicit legacy/description
  fallback, with the fallback documented and tested.
- `find-related` and `implement` are updated first (as named in the parent
  request) to use the AC rows rather than a full `wl show` where the table
  suffices.
- AC-coverage review (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::compute_coverage` /
  `apply_coverage_review`) compares criteria rows — by id where both sides are
  migrated, by similarity only for unmigrated descriptions — and its behaviour
  is covered by tests.
- Per-criterion status is honoured where the skills already reason about
  criteria (audit reports, plan coverage, intake briefs): a `met` criterion does
  not count as a gap, and a `modified` criterion is shown with its original text
  and justification.
- Skills remain functional against a store that has **not** yet run `wl doctor
  upgrade` (no AC rows): the fallback path is exercised by a test.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop re-parsing acceptance criteria out of prose and read them as
addressable rows with their own status, so a criterion can be cited by id and a
re-worded criterion is visibly `modified` rather than silently different.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the Worklog store beyond the existing `wl` CLI surface: no
  writes to the `acceptance_criteria` table from the skills.
- The skills ship from this repository; the table is delivered by ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG`. Do not implement schema or CLI changes here.
- `AC status is advisory in this phase` (ContextHub decision Q3 = advisory): no
  skill may gate closure on AC status yet — 15,172 back-filled criteria start as
  `unmet`.
- **Blocking dependency**: this work cannot be implemented until the ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (Add a table for ACs) delivers the `wl ac` CLI and
  back-fill. That item is `blocked`/`plan_complete`. This item must be marked
  blocked-on that dependency.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` parses prose from
  `## Acceptance Criteria` headings using regex/line-scanning.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py::run_wl_show` fetches a full
  `wl show` to read descriptions (and indirectly, AC prose).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` extracts AC lines internally and
  supports `adjusted` verdicts in its own vocabulary but does not yet use the
  AC table.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` accepts `acceptance_criteria` rows
  but only from the render_report CLI, not from skills.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`
  reference AC coverage via prose-parsed lists.

## Desired change

All skills that programmatically consume ACs delegate to `wl ac show <id> --json`
(or an equivalent table-read helper). Where the AC table is absent (pre-migration
stores), a documented fallback reads prose. AC-coverage comparison uses row ids
when available, falls back to string similarity when not.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Migration window risk:** Both prose-fallback and table-backed code paths must
  coexist during the transition. Any regression in prose-fallback will break
  skills against un-migrated stores.
  *Mitigation:* exhaustive fallback tests before table migration; phased rollout.
- **Scope creep:** All listed skills (tree_coverage, find-related, implement, plan,
  intake, audit, report) in a single change-set is large. Risk of merge conflicts
  and review fatigue.
  *Mitigation:* implement in dependency order (tree_coverage → find-related →
  implement → audit → report → skill docs).
- **Assumption:** the `wl ac show` CLI surface (JSON shape) stabilises before
  implementation begins. If it changes, the table-adapter in tree_coverage will
  need revision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — needs table-backed AC reads and the
  documented legacy fallback.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — needs AC rows instead of a
  full `wl show` where possible.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — needs the AC workflow to read rows.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — need the coverage/brief
  paths updated.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — needs its per-criterion verdicts
  reconciled with the table's status vocabulary (`adjusted` ≈ `modified`).
- `skill/shared/tests/` — needs coverage tests for table-backed reads plus the
  no-AC-rows fallback.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the `wl ac` CLI already available in the SorraAgents environment?"
  — Answer (research): No. `wl ac --help` is not found; the ContextHub item
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` is `blocked` / `plan_complete`. This is a hard block
  — implementation cannot start until ContextHub delivers.
- Q: "Which skills are in-scope for the initial table-backed migration?"
  — Answer (from description): `tree_coverage` (core), `find-related`,
  `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `audit`, `report`.

## Plan decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-26T23:42:45Z)

Decomposed into nine child items in dependency order: test-first harness first,
then the shared adapter, the table-aware coverage engine, the named consumers
(`find-related`, `implement`), `audit`, `report`, documentation, and finally the
legacy-store end-to-end regression gate.

| 1 | AC table fixtures and fake runner (SA-0MWY74267003UVSD) | task | WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG (foreign) |

## Problem statement

`run-release.js` bounds the canonical merge script with `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS`,
whose default is 600 s, but that script runs the **full test suite on the merged
dev→main tree** before bumping/tagging/pushing. On this repository the release
step takes ~33 min, so the 600 s default guarantees a kill on every release. The
kill leaves the **main checkout parked on an orphan `release/dev-to-main-*`
branch** carrying a partial version bump and CHANGELOG entry, with no tag, PR or
push to show for it — and the error message only tells the operator to "check
for partially-created branches".

## Users

- **Release operators (human):** run `/skill:ship release` and must not be left
  on a half-built release branch with a tree that a naive re-run would bump on
  top of.
- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases unattended; a timeout must
  end in a clean, known repository state it can retry from.
- **Example user story:** "As a release operator, when a release exceeds the
  wrapper's timeout, I want the checkout restored to `dev` and the orphan
  release branch removed automatically, reported clearly — so re-running the
  release starts from a clean state instead of stacking a second version bump."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapper's default release-script timeout is generous enough for a normal
  release on this repository: default `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS` ≥ 3 600 000 ms
  (60 min), justified against the observed 1 982 s Step 5 runtime, and still
  env-overridable (the bound from SA-0MSDX3KTV0092B7N is retained, only widened).
  A unit test asserts the default value and that the env override still wins.
- Before spawning the merge script the wrapper records the branch checked out at
  run start, and on a spawn timeout (`error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'`) it restores
  that branch in the main checkout, so the checkout is never left on a
  `release/dev-to-main-*` branch.
- On the same timeout path the wrapper deletes the orphan
  `release/dev-to-main-*` branch(es) that this run created, identified by
  diffing a pre-run branch snapshot against the post-timeout branch list rather
  than by a bare glob; a branch that was pushed to origin or referenced by an
  open PR is **not** deleted and is named in the message instead.
- The timeout error message names exactly what it restored and what it deleted
  (or refused to delete, with the reason), replacing the current
  "check for partially-created branches" wording; exit code 10 is retained and
  its description in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and
  `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` is updated.
- Tests cover the timeout-recovery path end to end against a temp repo with a
  fake hanging merge script that creates a `release/dev-to-main-*` branch:
  branch restored to the start branch, orphan branch gone, message names both,
  Code Freeze marker still cleared, and the normal (non-timeout) path unchanged.

## Impact

A release that outruns its timeout now leaves the checkout exactly where it
started, so operators can simply re-run instead of hand-recovering a half-bumped
release branch.

## Constraints

- **Exit codes are a documented contract:** the timeout path must keep exit
  code 10 (table in `skill/ship/SKILL.md`); no new exit codes.
- **Recovery must be conservative:** never delete a branch that exists on
  `origin` or backs an open PR; never `reset --hard` a start branch that has
  local commits — restoring the branch is required, discarding commits is not.
- **No concurrent-run interference:** identify orphans by pre/post branch
  snapshot, not by `release/dev-to-main-*` glob, so a parallel release in
  another checkout or a concurrently created branch is not touched.
- The Code Freeze marker's existing `finally` clearing must keep working on the
  timeout path.
- No behaviour change to `--dry-run`, gating steps or post-release steps.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js:62-63` —
  `const RELEASE_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS) || 600000;`
  introduced by SA-0MSDX3KTV0092B7N (bounded spawn) with the deliberately small
  10-minute default.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js:1947-1975` — Step 5 spawns
  `bash [selectedScript, ...forwardedArgs]` with `timeout: RELEASE_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS`;
  on `ETIMEDOUT` it prints the timeout message and `return finish(10)` with no
  repository recovery.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh:155-161` — creates
  `BRANCH="release/dev-to-main-$TIMESTAMP"` and `git checkout -b "$BRANCH" origin/main`;
  its only `trap` (line 110) clears the Code Freeze marker, not the branch. A
  SIGTERM mid-script therefore leaves the branch checked out.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js:1495-1520` — `syncDevWithMain()` already
  does `git checkout dev` (post-success only), so the wrapper has precedent for
  checkout management but no start-branch bookkeeping.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md:256` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md:76` document
  exit code 10 with "default 600s".
- `tests/unit/test-code-freeze-marker.mjs:266-311` — existing harness for the
  timeout path: a temp skill dir with a fake hanging `merge-dev-to-main.sh`,
  `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS: '500'`, asserting exit 10 and marker clearing. The
  new recovery tests extend this pattern.

## Desired change

1. Raise the default release-script timeout to a value sized for a real release
   (≥ 60 min), documented with the observed 1 982 s runtime as rationale, and
   keep the env override.
2. Snapshot the start branch (and the branch list) before the spawn; on
   `ETIMEDOUT`, restore the start branch, delete this run's orphan
   `release/dev-to-main-*` branch when it is unpushed and PR-free, and report
   precisely what happened in the exit-10 message.
3. Update the exit-code documentation and add the timeout-recovery tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — raise the default timeout; add start-branch/branch-snapshot capture around the Step 5 spawn and a
  `recoverFromReleaseTimeout` helper; enrich the exit-10 message.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — only if the wrapper needs a
  machine-readable hint (e.g. echo the branch name it checked out); no behaviour
  change expected otherwise.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — exit code 10 row: new default and recovery behaviour.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — same exit-code table update.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-timeout-recovery.mjs` (new, or extend
  `tests/unit/test-code-freeze-marker.mjs`) — timeout recovery assertions plus a
  default-timeout assertion.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the widened default hides a genuine hang longer:** a truly stuck
  git/gh call now blocks the project-wide Code Freeze for up to the new default.
  Mitigation: keep the bound, emit a "still running after N s" progress line, and
  document the env override prominently.
- **Risk — recovery races a concurrent release:** deleting by glob could remove
  another run's branch. Mitigation: pre/post branch snapshot (already an AC) and
  skip branches present on `origin` or backing an open PR.
- **Risk — timeout arrives mid-`git checkout`:** a half-completed checkout can
  leave a detached/odd HEAD. Mitigation: restore-then-verify — report the actual
  post-recovery `HEAD` branch in the message, and fail with exit 10 either way
  rather than claiming success.
- **Assumption:** the release operator's shell starts releases from the main
  checkout on `dev`; recovery restores whatever branch was recorded, so a release
  started elsewhere is restored to *its* start branch rather than hard-coded
  `dev`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** fixing SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT's post-release cleanup
  non-determinism, or adding a `--release-timeout` CLI flag, is out of scope here
  — record such opportunities as linked work items instead of expanding this one.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSDX3KTV0092B7N** (completed) — added the bounded spawn and the 600 s
  default this item relaxes; this is the direct predecessor.
- **SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT** (open, `plan_complete`) — ship post-release branch
  cleanup is non-deterministic (shared `/tmp` report path). Adjacent but
  distinct: that item is *post-success* local/remote branch cleanup, this one is
  *timeout-path* recovery in the main checkout. Implementation should avoid
  reusing the shared temp-path pattern it describes.
- **SA-0MS95HJ0J004IDIW** (completed) — precedent for widening a ship timeout
  that spuriously aborted releases.
- **SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS** — merge-verification guard; same fail-closed philosophy
  of never letting a release step proceed on unverified state.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed)
- **SA-0MQAUIMBT009351X** – Post-release dev sync: return to dev and merge main after ship (completed)
- **SA-0MPVK6RMQ008PYZ6** – Remediate skill: ship — make script references skill-relative and defensive (completed)

> The automated matches above are low-signal (keyword overlap on generic release
> vocabulary); the hand-curated "Related work" list is the authoritative one for

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Should the timeout default be a fixed generous constant or dynamically
  derived from the measured full-suite runtime?
  **Answer (agent, routine — documented assumption):** fixed generous constant
  (≥ 60 min) plus env override. A measured estimate would need a full-suite run
  before every release (extra 30+ min) and would still be a guess; the operator
  already demonstrated 5 400 000 ms works. Recorded as an assumption, reversible
  cheaply (one constant + docs).
  **Evidence:** item description (run 2 used `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS=5400000`
  successfully), `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js:63`.
- **Q:** Should recovery also `reset --hard` a dirty start branch?
  **Answer (agent, routine — documented assumption):** no. Restoring the branch
  satisfies the reported symptom; a hard reset could destroy unrelated local
  work. The refusal is documented in the message instead.
  **Evidence:** item's "Expected" §2 asks only for restoring the branch and
  deleting the orphan.
- **Q:** Is this the same defect as SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT?
  **Answer (agent, routine — duplicate check):** no. That item covers
  non-deterministic post-release branch cleanup via a shared temp path; this item
  covers the timeout path leaving the main checkout on an orphan branch. Both
  touch `run-release.js` branch handling, so they are linked as related work
  rather than merged.
  **Evidence:** `wl show SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT`, and the duplicate search performed
  for "release timeout", "run-release", "orphan release branch" — no completed
  item covers this timeout-recovery gap.

data.description:
# A failed dev→main sync aborts the verified post-release tail: the release ships but every item stays open and no notification is sent

## Problem statement

`run-release.js` runs the post-release tail in an order where the network-dependent
`syncDevWithMain()` (Step 7) executes **before** merge verification (Step 8), the Discord
notification (Step 8.5) and work-item closure (Step 9). A transport-only failure on that
single `git push origin dev` therefore returns `finish(5)` and silently discards the whole
verified tail — the release has already landed on `main`, yet no notification is sent and all
shipped items stay `completed/in_review`. There is also no supported way to finish a
partially-applied release: re-running `run-release.js` trips the newly-created-tag gate
(exit 14) by design.

## Users

- **Release manager (operator)** — runs `/skill:ship release` and needs a release that
  landed to be fully recorded, even when one later network call fails.
- **Autonomous release agent / driven session** — must not be left with a half-applied
  release it cannot legally finish with any supported command.
- **Producer** — relies on the Discord announcement and on shipped items reaching
  `completed/done` without manual `node -e` scripting.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when `git push origin dev` fails with "Connection to github.com
  closed by remote host", the release still verifies, announces and closes its items, and I
  am told exactly which single command re-syncs `dev`.
- As a release manager recovering a half-applied release (v0.2.0 on 2026-11-26), I run
  `node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --finish-release 0.2.0` and the tail
  completes idempotently without a new tag, merge or PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tail reordered so network-dependent work cannot suppress verified work.** The
   post-release order becomes: verify release merge (gating) → Discord notification →
   close work items → branch cleanup → sync dev with main **last**. Existing gates are
   preserved unchanged: a failed `verifyReleaseMerge` still exits 11 before any
   notification or close, and the newly-created-tag gate still exits 14 before any
   post-release step.
2. **A dev-sync failure is non-fatal.** When `syncDevWithMain()` fails after the tail has
   run, the run completes with exit code 0 (the release *did* land), prints a loud
   `⚠️` warning naming the failure and the exact recovery command (`git push origin dev`),
   and reports the sync outcome in the timing/summary output. Exit code 5 is no longer
   emitted by a full release run (documented as reserved).
3. **Dev sync retries transient transport errors.** `syncDevWithMain()` retries only
   transport-class failures (connection reset/closed by remote host, TLS/proxy errors,
   timeouts) — default 3 attempts with exponential backoff — and does not retry
   deterministic failures (merge conflict, non-fast-forward rejection, missing ref).
   Attempts/backoff are injectable so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real
   repository.
4. **`--finish-release <version>` completes a partially-applied tail idempotently.** The new
   entry point runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync —
   with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump, no Code Freeze marker, and
   without tripping the newly-created-tag gate (provenance comes from
   `verifyReleaseMerge` instead). It exits 0 on success, 11 when merge verification fails,
   13 on an invalid/unknown argument, and nothing is executed on argument error.
5. **Notification provenance is explicit on the recovery path.** `sendReleaseNotification`
   keeps failing closed by default (a pre-existing tag is never announced); the
   `--finish-release` path supplies the verified-release provenance explicitly so a
   confirmed release is announced exactly once, and re-running it does not double-notify
   (or the duplicate is documented and accepted).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: tail ordering (verify/notify/close before dev sync, and
   dev-sync failure not aborting them), transport-only retry policy (retries then
   succeeds; deterministic failure not retried), the `--finish-release` entry point
   (gate bypass, exit codes, no merge/PR/tag calls, argument-error inertness) and
   idempotent re-run. Existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` and
   `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stay green.
7. **Documentation.** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (post-release step order, exit-code table,
   partial-release recovery section) and `docs/dev/release-process.md` (recovery runbook)
   describe the new order, the non-fatal dev sync and the `--finish-release` command.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A release that already landed can no longer be left half-applied: a transient network
reset on the final `dev` push no longer costs the announcement and the closure of every
shipped item, and an operator has one documented command that finishes the tail instead of
hand-rolled `node -e` scripts.

## Constraints

- **Purely internal tooling surface.** No work-item data-model, worklog-store or
  notification-format change; `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` reload/close semantics stay as
  they are.
- **Existing safety gates must not weaken.** The newly-created-tag gate (exit 14) and
  `verifyReleaseMerge` (exit 11) stay hard gates for a normal release; `--finish-release`
  may bypass *only* the tag-creation gate, and only because it proves the release by
  origin-tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main` verification instead.
- **No new dependencies**; the retry/backoff must not make unit tests slow (injectable
  clock/sleep).
- **Worktree/main-checkout rule unchanged:** release operations still run from the main
  checkout, never from a worktree.

## Evidence (original report)

- `/tmp/ship-release7.log`: `⚠️  Failed to sync dev with main: … Connection to github.com
  closed by remote host.`; the timing table shows `Step 7: sync dev with main 0.000` and no
  Steps 8-10.
- PR #730 merged, tag `v0.2.0` created, `origin/main` = `ad34d578cd` — the release landed,
  yet items stayed `completed/in_review` (e.g. SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK, SA-0MWFP1E9P0027EOE) and
  were closed manually by importing `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in a one-off node script.
- Re-running `run-release.js` was impossible: `v0.2.0` already existed, so the
  newly-created-tag gate would exit 14 by design.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (2134 lines): Step 7 `syncDevWithMain()` at ~line
  2013 returning `finish(5)`; Step 8 verify/tag gate at ~2056; Step 8.5 notification at
  ~2084; Step 9 close at ~2092; Step 10 cleanup after. Arg parsing via `BOOLEAN_FLAGS` /
  `VALUE_FLAGS` / `parseReleaseArgs()` (exit 13 on unknown flag) at ~line 145-250; a
  pre-flight-only early-exit precedent (`--refresh-audits` → `runRefreshAuditsAction`)
  at ~line 1743.
- `syncDevWithMain(options)` already takes an injectable `options.run` command runner
  (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) — the retry loop can reuse that seam.
- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` is already idempotent (`Shipped in v<version>` marker,
  version-exact, SA-0MUECDK14002J37J) and verifies persisted closure.
- `sendReleaseNotification()` already fails closed on provenance (`preRunTags`).
- No `--finish-release` / resume path exists anywhere (verified by repo grep).

## Desired change

1. Move the `syncDevWithMain()` call after verify → notify → close → cleanup; make its
   failure a warning that does not change the exit code.
2. Wrap the sync's command runner in a bounded retry for transport-class errors.
3. Add `--finish-release <version>`: parse it as a value flag, route it to a new
   `runFinishReleaseAction(flags)` **before** `setCodeFreezeMarker`/`runReleaseImpl`
   (mirroring `--refresh-audits`), and have it run the tail with an explicit
   verified-release provenance and no tag gate.
4. Update `WRAPPER_USAGE`, the SKILL.md exit-code table + release-process step list, and
   add a partial-release recovery section to `docs/dev/release-process.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — reorder the tail (~2007-2115); add the retry loop
  to `syncDevWithMain` (~1495); add `--finish-release` to `VALUE_FLAGS`, `parseReleaseArgs`,
  `WRAPPER_USAGE` (~145-250); add `runFinishReleaseAction` and its call site next to the
  `--refresh-audits` pre-flight (~1743); add the non-fatal dev-sync warning.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — add/confirm an explicit provenance option so a
  verified `--finish-release` can announce without a pre-run tag snapshot.
- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` — retry-policy and ordering coverage
  (injected runner/sleep).
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-finish-release.mjs` *(new)* — entry-point behaviour, exit
  codes, no merge/PR/tag side effects, idempotent re-run, argument-error inertness.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` *(new)* — verified tail ordering and
  dev-sync failure not suppressing notify/close.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — exit-code table (5 reserved), release-process step order,
  recovery section for `--finish-release`.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — partially-applied release recovery runbook.

## Related work

- **SA-0MQAUIMBT009351X** — Post-release dev sync: return to dev and merge main after ship
  (completed): introduced `syncDevWithMain()`, the step this item re-orders and retries.
- **SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA** — Gate post-release steps on a newly created tag (completed):
  source of the exit-14 gate that makes a re-run of a partially-applied release impossible
  today; this item adds the supported recovery path *around* that gate.
- **SA-0MUECDK14002J37J** — Run-release close idempotency (`Shipped in v<version>` marker,
  completed): makes re-running the close step safe, a precondition for `--finish-release`.
- **SA-0MV0QEI3Q0063KH3** — Discord announcement provenance guard (completed): the fail-closed
  notifier behaviour the recovery path must supply provenance for.
- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** — Test infra: concurrent full-suite runs deadlock (completed):
  gave `syncDevWithMain`/`verifyReleaseMerge` the injectable command-runner seam reused here.
- **SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT** — Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically
  (open): same non-blocking-tail area; independent failure mode, no overlap in fix.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — the documentation surface
  describing the tail order and exit codes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Should a dev-sync failure keep a non-zero exit code (today's `5`)? **Recommended:**
  exit 0 with a warning — a landed release is a success, and a non-zero code would let
  automation misreport the release as failed. — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):**
  exit 0 with a `⚠️` warning naming `git push origin dev`; exit 5 documented as reserved.
  Source: work item "Expected" item 1 ("must not be fatal to the release result");
  research: existing codes 2/4/5/6/7/9/10/11/12/13/14 in `skill/ship/SKILL.md`.
- **Q:** How many retry attempts and which errors are retryable? **Recommended:** 3 attempts,
  exponential backoff, transport-class errors only. — **Answer (agent, documented
  assumption):** as recommended; backoff/attempts injectable for tests. Source: work item
  item 2; research: `syncDevWithMain` already exposes `options.run`
  (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86).
- **Q:** Should `--finish-release` bypass the newly-created-tag gate? **Recommended:** yes,
  substituting `verifyReleaseMerge` (origin tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main`) as provenance.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** yes; the gate exists to stop *spurious*
  releases, and the recovery path proves the release by the origin/ancestor facts instead.
  Source: work item item 3; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` § Newly-created-tag gate.
- **Q:** Can re-running `--finish-release` double-post the Discord announcement?
  **Recommended:** accept at-most-once semantics from the existing notifier and document
  idempotence for close/cleanup/sync only. — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):**
  recommended; note it in the SKILL.md recovery section because no send-marker exists.
  Research: `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` has no dedupe store.
- **Q:** Is a separate work item needed for idempotent notification (a sent-marker)?
  **Recommended:** no — record as an out-of-scope opportunity. — **Answer (agent):** recorded
  as a scope-creep risk below, not created (single-operator tool, low value today).

### Plan round (2026-11-26)

- **Q:** How should the change be decomposed — (a) 6 children as 3 test/verification items then 3 implementation items, (b) 3 children each carrying its own tests, (c) 1 item for the whole description?
  **Recommended:** (a) — the plan skill requires test/verification items before implementation items, and the three behaviours have independent test files.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" — no objection raised, so the recommendation was adopted: **final (a)**. Source: plan interview round 1, this work item's session `herdr-1795698218-2137099-6223`.
- **Q:** Transport-error classification for the retry — (a) allowlist (retry only recognised transport signatures; anything unrecognised is not retried) vs (b) denylist (retry everything except known-deterministic failures)?
  **Recommended:** (a) — `git merge` is not idempotent, so an unknown failure must fail closed rather than be replayed.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" → **final (a)** allowlist. Recorded in child SA-0MWXMTQ4Q001N0WJ.
- **Q:** Where do the documentation updates land — (a) folded into the implementation children (vertical slices) or (b) one separate docs child depending on both?
  **Recommended:** (a) — the plan skill's vertical-slice rule; a standalone docs item would be a horizontal layer.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" → **final (a)**; step order + exit-code reservations go with the reorder child, the recovery runbook + `WRAPPER_USAGE` with the `--finish-release` child.
- **Q:** Test-first children cannot commit failing tests (the changed-scope gate must be green), so how do the red-first halves land?
  **Recommended:** commit the new tests with `node:test`'s `{ todo: true }` — the analogue of the `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` red-first pattern already used in this repository.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** as recommended. Research: `git show a45899877` (child SA-0MW3GCHEL001G8CP) shows the xfail red-first pattern; `node:test` has no xfail, and `{ todo: true }` is the closest fail-safe equivalent (a failing todo test does not fail the run). Each implementation child removes its marker.
- **Q:** Where does the retry classifier live, and does a retry replay the whole command sequence?
  **Recommended:** classifier + inner `attemptSync()` next to `syncDevWithMain()`, with every attempt restarting from a fresh `git fetch origin --prune`.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** as recommended — a retried merge must never compound stale state; the existing `options.run` seam (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) carries the fake runner.
- **Q:** Should the notifier gain a sent-marker so `--finish-release` re-runs never double-announce?
  **Recommended:** no — out of scope (see the existing Appendix entry above), documented as at-most-once.
  — **Answer (agent):** unchanged from the intake Appendix; not re-asked. No child created for a dedupe store.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** touching the notifier could grow into building an announcement
  dedupe/marker store — explicitly out of scope; only the provenance plumbing changes.
- **Gate weakening risk:** a bug in `--finish-release` routing could let a normal release
  skip the exit-14 gate. Mitigation: the flag is only honoured by the recovery action
  before `runReleaseImpl` is entered; the normal path's gate is untouched, and a unit test
  asserts it still fires.
- **Reordering risk:** moving `syncDevWithMain` last changes repository state during the
  close/cleanup steps (still on the release branch, `main` not yet merged into `dev`) —
  mitigated because those steps operate on tags/`origin/main`, not the local checkout.
- **Retry risk:** retrying a non-idempotent `git merge` could compound state. Mitigation:
  retry only transport-class errors, re-running the full command sequence from a fresh
  fetch, and never retry conflicts/rejections.
- **Assumption:** a partially-applied release is detectable by the operator from the run
  output/timing report (no new persisted state file is introduced).
## Plan: decomposition (2026-11-26)

Six children — three red-first test items then three implementation items — all
priority `critical`, mapped to the ACs above. Deps: `2←1`, `4←3,2`, `6←5,2`.

| # | Child | Type | Parent ACs | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|------------|
| 1 | Test: tail order and non-fatal dev sync (SA-0MWXMTERQ005HYQ3) | task | 1, 2, 6 | — |
| 2 | Reorder post-release tail, sync dev last (SA-0MWXMTNIV006TJH5) | bug | 1, 2, 7, 8 | 1 |
| 3 | Test: transport-only dev sync retry (SA-0MWXMTIM7006760U) | task | 3, 6 | — |
| 4 | Retry transport errors in dev sync (SA-0MWXMTQ4Q001N0WJ) | bug | 3 | 3, 2 |
| 5 | Test: finish-release recovery entry point (SA-0MWXMTKYB006IBPK) | task | 4, 5, 6 | 2 |
| 6 | Add --finish-release recovery command (SA-0MWXMTSKH0085UZZ) | feature | 4, 5, 7, 8 | 5, 2 |

Execution order: **1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6** (`wl next` resolves it).

**Design decisions**

- The verified tail is extracted into `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({version, prUrl, projectRoot, dryRun, provenance})` so the normal path and the recovery path share one ordering; `runReleaseImpl` loses its duplicated Steps 8-10.
- Retry classification is an **allowlist** of transport signatures (connection reset / closed by remote host, `RPC failed`, `early EOF`, TLS/proxy, DNS, timeouts) — an unknown error is never replayed because `git merge` is not idempotent.
- Test-first children land their tests with `node:test`'s `{ todo: true }` (the `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` analogue used by SA-0MW3GCHEL001G8CP); the matching implementation child removes the marker.
- Docs ride along with their slice: the reorder child updates the SKILL.md step order and reserves exit code 5; the `--finish-release` child adds the exit-code table entries, recovery section and `docs/dev/release-process.md` runbook.
- Notification dedupe on re-run stays out of scope (documented at-most-once); no sent-marker store is introduced.
- Related, non-overlapping: SA-0MWXIXV2R008MRT3 (wrapper timeout leaves the main checkout on an orphan release branch) — independent failure mode, no shared fix.

**Vertical-slice note:** the three test items are deliberately test-only — they are the red-first halves of three vertical slices, per the plan skill's test-first ordering rule. Every implementation item carries code + tests + docs. Between phases, re-read the next child's description: child 2 lands the shared helper that children 4 and 6 build on.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-26 — Planning run: decomposed into 6 test-first children, wired deps, AC coverage verified at 100% by the shared tree-coverage review, effort/risk re-estimated.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA** – Gate post-release steps on a newly created tag (completed)
- **SA-0MQAUIMBT009351X** – Post-release dev sync: return to dev and merge main after ship (completed)
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0muy6u05f008rg86, 0mwffx49m0016kok, aborting, aborts, accept (+396 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mwffx49m0016kok, aborting, aborts, accept, acceptance (+389 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, aborts, accept, acceptance, accepted (+366 more)

data.description:
## Goal

As a workflow operator, I want the intake skill's closing stage to apply the
same effort/risk pre-check rules that the plan skill uses, so that an item
which does not need planning is advanced straight to `plan_complete` at the
end of intake instead of being left at `intake_complete` for a separate plan
session that would only rubber-stamp it.

**User story:** When intake finishes an item whose effort and risk are below
the planning threshold, the item should land at `plan_complete` without a
redundant `/skill:plan` run.

## Context

The plan skill has a pre-check (`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`, exposed as
`plan-if-needed` and importable as `plan_if_needed` / `make_autoplan_decision`)
that decides whether planning can be skipped:

- Skip only when **both**: effort in `{"Extra Small", "Small"}`
  (`DEFAULT_AUTOPLAN_EFFORT_SKIP`) **and** risk in `{"Low"}`
  (`DEFAULT_AUTOPLAN_RISK_SKIP`).
- Any other combination → `plan`.
- Unknown/absent estimates (no real inputs) → fall back to `plan` (never skip
  silently).
- Fetch error → `error`, which callers must treat as `plan` (fail-safe).

Intake already computes effort and risk in its closing sequence
(`skill/intake/SKILL.md` step 10, `orchestrate_estimate.py`), so the pre-check
inputs are available immediately before finishing (step 11). Today intake
always stops at `intake_complete`, even when the pre-check would return
`skip`.

## Desired change

Add a closing step to the intake skill (after the effort/risk estimate and
before the finishing step) that:

1. Runs the canonical autoplan pre-check for the work item.
2. If the decision is `skip`, advances the stage to `plan_complete` (status
   `open`, assignee released per the assignee-release invariant) and records a
   comment naming the decision.
3. If the decision is `plan`, `error`, or the estimates are unknown/absent,
   leaves the stage at `intake_complete` (fail-safe: planning still runs).
4. Is idempotent: re-running intake on an item already at `plan_complete` or
   later must not regress the stage.

**Helper reuse / extraction.** Do not duplicate the threshold logic. Reuse the
canonical logic already in `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`. If a direct
intake → plan skill import is considered undesirable, extract the decision
module into `skill/shared/` and have both `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` and the
intake step import it (keeping the existing plan CLI and tests working). The
extraction choice and rationale must be recorded in the work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The intake skill's closing sequence invokes the autoplan pre-check after the effort/risk estimate and before the finishing step.
2. When the pre-check decision is `skip`, the work item's stage is advanced to `plan_complete`, status is `open`, and the assignee is released.
3. When the decision is `plan`, `error`, or the effort/risk estimate is unknown/absent, the stage remains `intake_complete` (fail-safe, no silent skip).
4. Re-running intake on an item already at `plan_complete` or later does not regress or re-open the stage (idempotent).
5. The threshold logic is single-sourced: intake consumes the same canonical helper as the plan skill (direct reuse or a shared extraction); no duplicated threshold constants.
6. Automated tests cover: skip → `plan_complete`; plan → `intake_complete`; unknown → `intake_complete`; error → `intake_complete`; and idempotence/no-regression.
7. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` document the new closing step and its fail-safe/idempotence rules.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — add the closing pre-check step and its fail-safe/idempotence rules.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — wire the pre-check into the closing CLI path (e.g. a `finish`/post-estimate step).
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — canonical autoplan decision logic (reuse, or move the decision core to `skill/shared/`).
- `skill/shared/` — new shared autoplan decision module if extraction is chosen.
- `skill/intake/tests/` — new tests for skip/plan/unknown/error/idempotence.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — maintainer reference for the new step.

## Notes / Constraints

- Do not change the plan skill's behaviour: an item that reaches `plan_complete` at intake end must be treated exactly as if plan had completed (the plan skill already returns `skip` for `plan_complete` via its idempotence check).
- Preserve the status/stage distinction: `plan_complete` is a stage; status becomes `open`.
- Follow the assignee-release invariant — no lingering `Intake` (or other) assignee after the transition.
- Keep the change minimal and test-first; use `replace`-style mocks consistent with existing `skill/intake/tests/` patterns so no live `wl` store is required.
- Motivation: recent plan-session analysis showed the skip-path review stages rarely change anything, so an item that the pre-check already deems planning-free should not need a separate plan session.

## Impact

Skip redundant planning sessions for low-effort, low-risk items when they come out of intake, eliminating unnecessary intermediate steps in the workflow.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MW0LPXXY0002CQ0** — Autoplan effort/risk fallback stamps 0h / Extra Small / Low on an epic, silently skipping planning. Related to threshold logic safety.
- **SA-0MSIUJQAK008AQV8** — plan-if-needed silently corrupts work-item effort/risk when worklog lookup fails. Related error-handling concern in the same helper module.
- **SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ** — Ralph loop auto plan if necessary. Related auto-planning effort at intake_complete stage.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Adding the pre-check to intake SKILL.md affects all future intake sessions. Mitigation: the check is conservative (fail-safe) and idempotent.
- **Import coupling:** Direct intake→plan skill import could create a dependency cycle. Mitigation: extract decision core to `skill/shared/` if import coupling is a concern.
- **Threshold misconfiguration:** If `DEFAULT_AUTOPLAN_EFFORT_SKIP` or `DEFAULT_AUTOPLAN_RISK_SKIP` values are misconfigured, items could be incorrectly skipped. Mitigation: the fallback is `plan` (never skip silently).
- **Assumption:** The plan skill's idempotence check (returning `skip` for `plan_complete`) already handles the `plan_complete`-at-intake-end case.
- **Assumption:** Tests can mock the plan helper without requiring a live worklog store, consistent with existing `skill/intake/tests/` patterns.

## Goal

Raise the release-script default timeout and add start-branch bookkeeping plus `ETIMEDOUT` recovery to the ship wrapper, so a timed-out release leaves the main checkout in its original state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapper's default `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS` is ≥ 3 600 000 ms (60 min), justified against the observed 1 982 s Step 5 runtime, and remains env-overridable.
- Before spawning the merge script, the wrapper records the checked-out branch and the branch list.
- On `ETIMEDOUT`, the wrapper restores that branch in the main checkout so it is never left on a `release/dev-to-main-*` branch.
- On the same timeout path, the wrapper deletes the orphan `release/dev-to-main-*` branch(es) created by this run — identified by pre/post branch-snapshot diff, not a bare glob. A branch pushed to origin or referenced by an open PR is NOT deleted and is named in the message.
- The timeout error message names exactly what it restored and what it deleted (or refused to delete, with the reason), replacing the current wording; exit code 10 is retained.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` exit-code-10 descriptions are updated to reflect the new default and recovery behaviour.

## Constraints

- Exit code 10 stays the documented timeout contract; no new exit codes.
- Never delete a branch that exists on `origin` or backs an open PR; never `reset --hard` a start branch with local commits.
- Identify orphans by pre/post branch snapshot (no concurrent-run interference).
- The Code Freeze marker's existing `finally` clearing must keep working.
- No behaviour change to `--dry-run`, gating steps or post-release steps.

# Test: tail order and non-fatal dev sync

TDD-first child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC1, AC2, AC6). Writes the
red-first regression harness that pins the corrected post-release tail order
and the non-fatal dev-sync contract **before** the reorder item lands, so the
reorder is test-driven.

## Context

Today `run-release.js` calls `syncDevWithMain()` at Step 7 (~line 2013) and
`return finish(5)` on failure — before merge verification (~2056), the Discord
notification (~2084), item closure (~2092) and cleanup (~2105). The observed
2026-11-26 release (`v0.2.0`, PR #730) landed on `main` yet the tail never ran:
`/tmp/ship-release7.log` shows `Step 7: sync dev with main 0.000` and no
Steps 8-10, leaving shipped items `completed/in_review`.

Reuse the existing harness pattern from
`tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`: copy the real
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` into a temp skill layout, put mocked
`git`/`wl`/`gh` binaries on `PATH` that append every invocation to one recorded
event log, and substitute the shared `tests/helpers/release-notify-stub.mjs`
for `discord-notify.js` (never copy the real notifier —
WL-0MUYA98Z8003HU8X).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` runs the real `run-release.js` in a temp skill layout with mocked `git`/`gh` binaries and the shared `release-notify-stub.mjs`, appending every step invocation to one shared event log.
- The recorded post-release order is: verify release merge → Discord notification → close work items → branch cleanup → sync dev with main last.
- A `git push origin dev` failure ("Connection to github.com closed by remote host") still completes with exit code 0, with the notification and the close calls recorded, and a `⚠️` warning naming the failure and the exact recovery command `git push origin dev` on stderr.
- A failed `verifyReleaseMerge` still exits 11 with no notification and no close recorded (existing gate preserved unchanged).
- An already-present release tag still exits 14 with no post-release step recorded (newly-created-tag gate preserved unchanged).
- The parent tests requirement is satisfied collectively by this item, the retry-policy test item and the `--finish-release` test item: unit tests cover tail ordering (verify/notify/close before dev sync, and dev-sync failure not aborting them), transport-only retry policy (retries then succeeds; deterministic failure not retried), the `--finish-release` entry point (gate bypass, exit codes, no merge/PR/tag calls, argument-error inertness) and idempotent re-run; existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` and `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stay green.

- Mocked `git` records `describe --tags`, `tag --list`, `fetch`, `checkout`, `merge`, `push`, `rev-parse`; mocked `wl` records close commands; the notifier stub records the announce.
- One assertion helper checks an ordered subsequence over the shared event log (order assertions, not exact-sequence assertions, so unrelated steps stay free).

A half-applied release is now caught by an automated regression test instead of by the next real release.

# Test: transport-only dev sync retry

TDD-first child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC3, AC6). Pins the retry policy
of `syncDevWithMain()` **before** the retry loop is implemented: transport-class
failures retry with exponential backoff, deterministic failures never do.

## Context

`syncDevWithMain(options)` already takes an injectable `options.run` command
runner (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 — the seam
`tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` already exercises at its
`syncDevWithMain (hermetic)` describe block). The retry loop reuses that seam
and adds an injectable sleep so tests never sleep and never touch a real
repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` gains a retry-policy describe block driving the real `syncDevWithMain()` through the existing injectable `options.run` seam plus an injected `options.sleep`, so no test sleeps and no real repository is touched.
- Transport-class failures are retried then succeed: a run whose first two attempts throw a transport error and whose third succeeds returns `{ success: true }`, records exactly 3 attempts, and the injected sleep is called twice with increasing delays.
- Deterministic failures are not retried: a runner throwing a merge conflict, a non-fast-forward `[rejected]` push or a missing-ref error produces exactly one attempt, no sleep call and `{ success: false }`.
- The default of 3 attempts with exponential backoff is asserted, and `options.attempts` / `options.backoffMs` / `options.sleep` override it.
- Each retry restarts the full command sequence from a fresh `git fetch origin --prune` before `checkout` / `merge` / `push` (asserted over the recorded command list).
- The new tests are committed with `{ todo: true }` on `node:test` (the red-first analogue of `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)`, mirroring SA-0MW3GCHEL001G8CP) so the changed-scope gate stays green; the retry implementation item removes the marker.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the existing `syncDevWithMain (hermetic)` coverage in `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` with a `retry policy` describe block.
- Build a command-logging fake runner factory: `(failuresByCommand, errorText)` → `{ run, calls }`.
- One helper builds a transport failure (`Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` / `Connection reset by peer`), another a deterministic one (`CONFLICT (content): merge conflict`, `! [rejected] dev -> dev (non-fast-forward)`, `couldn't find remote ref`).
- Mark the retry/deterministic assertions `{ todo: true }` until the implementation lands.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` — new retry-policy coverage
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `syncDevWithMain()` (~1477-1530), behaviour under test (read-only for this item)

## Impact

The retry behaviour is fixed by an automated test, so a future change cannot silently start replaying a non-idempotent merge.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the tail reorder so both items touching `run-release.js` land serially.

# Reorder post-release tail, sync dev last

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8). Makes the
network-dependent `dev` sync the **last** post-release step and its failure
non-fatal, so a verified release can never be suppressed by one transport
error.

## Context

`runReleaseImpl()` currently runs `syncDevWithMain()` as Step 7 and returns
`finish(5)` when it fails, before verify (Step 8), notify (8.5), close (9) and
cleanup (10). Exit code 5 has no other producer in the pipeline. The tail is
also duplicated logic that the sibling `--finish-release` recovery item must
reuse, so extract it as one exported helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The post-release order becomes: verify release merge (gating) → Discord notification → close work items → branch cleanup → sync dev with main last, so network-dependent work cannot suppress verified work.
- Existing gates are preserved unchanged: a failed `verifyReleaseMerge` still exits 11 before any notification or close, and the newly-created-tag gate still exits 14 before any post-release step.
- When `syncDevWithMain()` fails after the tail has run, the run completes with exit code 0 (the release *did* land), prints a loud `⚠️` warning naming the failure and the exact recovery command `git push origin dev`, and reports the sync outcome in the timing/summary output; exit code 5 is no longer emitted by a full release run and is documented as reserved.
- The verified tail is extracted into an exported `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({ version, prUrl, projectRoot, dryRun })` helper reused verbatim by the recovery entry point, with a `sync` outcome in its result object; normal-path ordering, notification, closure and cleanup behaviour are unchanged apart from the sync move.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` documents the new numbered step order, the non-fatal dev sync and exit code 5 as reserved, and existing code comments describing the old order are corrected.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `README.md` entries and any relevant docs-site or wiki references to the old tail order.
- The sibling ordering harness `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` loses its `todo` markers and passes, and the existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` and `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stay green.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `runReleaseImpl()`, delete the Step 7 block (~2007-2016) and run the sync **after** the Step 10 cleanup, inside the `if (version)` block, keeping the `stepTimers` entries and appending the sync row to the timing report.
- Wrap the call so a failure only logs `⚠️ Failed to sync dev with main: … Recover with: git push origin dev` and never changes the exit code.
- Extract Steps 8-10 plus the trailing sync into `export function runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` returning `{ version, notified, close, cleanup, sync }`; `runReleaseImpl` calls it and the sibling recovery item calls it too.
- Update `skill/ship/SKILL.md`'s numbered release-step list (steps 9-12 renumber to the new order) and its exit-code table (5 → reserved).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — tail reorder (~2007-2115), new `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` helper
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — release-process step order, exit-code table, dev-sync description
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — only the step-order references touched here; the recovery runbook belongs to the `--finish-release` item
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` — remove `todo` markers

## Impact

A transient network reset on the final `dev` push no longer costs the release its announcement and the closure of every shipped item.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the ordering harness (this item's tests must exist first).

# Retry transport errors in dev sync

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC3). Makes `syncDevWithMain()` retry
transport-class failures with exponential backoff, and only those.

## Context

The 2026-11-26 release died on `Connection to github.com closed by remote host`
— a transient transport fault that a retry would have absorbed. A `git merge`
is not idempotent, so classification must fail closed: an unrecognised error is
never replayed. Classification is therefore an **allowlist** of transport
signatures (documented assumption recorded in the parent Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dev sync retries transient transport errors: `syncDevWithMain()` retries only transport-class failures (connection reset/closed by remote host, `RPC failed`, `early EOF`, TLS/proxy errors, DNS resolution failures, timeouts) — default 3 attempts with exponential backoff — and does not retry deterministic failures (merge conflict, non-fast-forward rejection, missing ref). Attempts/backoff are injectable so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real repository; classification is a strict allowlist, so an unrecognised error is never replayed.
- Default is 3 attempts with exponential backoff, and attempts/backoff/sleep are injectable (`options.attempts`, `options.backoffMs`, `options.sleep`) so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real repository.
- Deterministic failures are never retried: merge conflict, non-fast-forward `[rejected]` push and missing ref each abort on the first attempt.
- Every retry restarts the full command sequence from a fresh `git fetch origin --prune`, and the exported `run()` default stays `execSync` with git output streamed to stderr.
- The returned `{ success, message }` names the attempt count and the last error; a success after retries reports how many attempts were needed, and the post-release timing/summary output surfaces it.
- The sibling retry test item's `todo` markers are removed and its tests pass, and `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stays green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments in `run-release.js` and the `skill/ship/SKILL.md` dev-sync description (retry policy and its scope).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `TRANSPORT_ERROR_PATTERNS` (case-insensitive regex list) and `isTransportError(err)` next to `syncDevWithMain()`.
- Extract the 4-command sequence into an inner `attemptSync()`; loop `for (attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1)` rethrowing non-transport errors immediately and sleeping `backoffMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)` between transport failures.
- Default `sleep` uses `Atomics.wait` on a `SharedArrayBuffer` (no dependency, no busy loop) and is injectable; validate `attempts >= 1`.
- Return `{ success, message, attempts }`; document the allowlist in a JSDoc block citing SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `syncDevWithMain()` (~1477-1530) plus the classifier helpers
- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` — remove `todo` markers
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — dev-sync step description mentions the retry policy

## Impact

A transient git transport error on the post-release sync is absorbed automatically instead of needing manual recovery.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the retry test item, and serialised after the tail reorder (both edit `run-release.js`).

# Add --finish-release recovery command

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC4, AC5, AC7, AC8). Adds the supported
`--finish-release <version>` entry point that completes a partially-applied
release tail without a new merge, PR, tag, version bump or Code Freeze marker.

## Context

A release that landed but whose tail never ran (the 2026-11-26 `v0.2.0` case)
cannot legally be finished today: re-running `run-release.js` trips the
newly-created-tag gate (exit 14, SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA). Provenance for the
recovery path comes from `verifyReleaseMerge()` (origin tag + ancestor of
`origin/main`) instead of the pre-run tag snapshot. `sendReleaseNotification`
already accepts an explicit `{ tagCreatedByThisRun }` provenance flag and must
keep failing closed by default (SA-0MV0QEI3Q0063KH3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `--finish-release <version>` is added to `VALUE_FLAGS`, `parseReleaseArgs()` and `WRAPPER_USAGE`, and routes to a new `runFinishReleaseAction(flags)` **before** `setCodeFreezeMarker`/`runReleaseImpl`, mirroring the `--refresh-audits` pre-flight early exit.
- The action runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync — through the shared `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` helper, with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump and no Code Freeze marker.
- The newly-created-tag gate is bypassed on this path only, because the action proves the release by origin-tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main` verification instead; a normal release's exit-14 and exit-11 gates are untouched and still fire.
- `--finish-release <version>` completes a partially-applied tail idempotently: the new entry point runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync — with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump, no Code Freeze marker, and without tripping the newly-created-tag gate (provenance comes from `verifyReleaseMerge` instead). It exits 0 on success, 11 when merge verification fails, 13 on an invalid/unknown argument, and nothing is executed on argument error.
- Notification provenance is explicit on the recovery path: `sendReleaseNotification` keeps failing closed by default (a pre-existing tag is never announced); the `--finish-release` path supplies the verified-release provenance explicitly (`{ tagCreatedByThisRun: true }` once `verifyReleaseMerge` succeeds) so a confirmed release is announced exactly once, and re-running it does not double-notify (the duplicate is documented and accepted — at-most-once, no dedupe store).
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` gains the exit-code table entries (5 reserved, `--finish-release`, 11, 13) plus a partial-release recovery section, and `docs/dev/release-process.md` gains the recovery runbook for `node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --finish-release <version>`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `README.md` and any relevant docs-site or wiki entries.
- The sibling `--finish-release` test item's `todo` markers are removed and its tests pass; existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` stay green.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Parse the flag into `flags.finishRelease`, validate it is a non-empty semver-ish string (else exit 13 before any side effect).
- Add `export async function runFinishReleaseAction(flags, projectRoot)` in the pre-flight area next to `runRefreshAuditsAction`'s call site (~1743): resolve root read-only, call `verifyReleaseMerge(version)` (exit 11 on failure), then `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({ version, prUrl: null, projectRoot, dryRun, provenance: { tagCreatedByThisRun: true } })`.
- Thread a `provenance` argument through `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` into `sendReleaseNotification` so the normal path still passes `{ preRunTags }` while the recovery path passes `{ tagCreatedByThisRun: true }`.
- Document the command, its exit codes, the at-most-once notification caveat and the recovery runbook in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/release-process.md`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `VALUE_FLAGS` / `parseReleaseArgs()` / `WRAPPER_USAGE` (~145-250), `runFinishReleaseAction()` next to the `--refresh-audits` pre-flight (~1743)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — confirm `{ tagCreatedByThisRun }` is sufficient; no dedupe store added (explicitly out of scope)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — exit-code table, post-release step order, partial-release recovery section
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — recovery runbook
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-finish-release.mjs` — remove `todo` markers

## Impact

A release that already landed can be finished with one documented command instead of a hand-rolled `node -e` script, so shipped items reach `completed/done` and the announcement goes out.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the `--finish-release` test item and the tail reorder (reuses `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()`).

## Goal

Stop work items staying `blocked` after every dependency edge they hold is `completed`, so `wl next` can dispatch them.

## Problem

Observed twice on the same leaf (2026-11-18 and 2026-11-26): `SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5` (child of SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1) was `blocked` while its only outbound edge `SA-0MWJ7K962006646G` was `completed`. A stale `blocked` hides a ready leaf from `wl next` and from downtime dispatch, so the plan run had to repair the status by hand each time. Something re-derives `blocked` (bulk re-derivation after dependency edits or sync) without re-checking whether the blocking edges are already satisfied.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduction recorded: the code path that sets `blocked` without re-validating completed outbound edges is identified (candidate: bulk status re-derivation in the worklog sync/import path).
2. When every outbound dependency edge of a `blocked` item is `completed`, the item is reconciled to `open` (or its documented ready status) — either at derivation time or by an idempotent sweep — without operator intervention.
3. Items with at least one unmet or missing edge stay `blocked`; `completed`/`deleted` items are never reopened.
4. Targeted tests cover: all-deps-completed `blocked` → reconciled; one-dep-open `blocked` → unchanged; already-`open` item → unchanged (idempotence).
5. Existing adjacent behaviour (SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2 block re-validation at start, SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW skip-blocked classification) keeps passing.

## Impact

Ready leaves stop disappearing from the dispatch queue because of a stale `blocked` status.

# Test: large-parent Phase 2 prompt-size capture contract

## Goal

Pin the prompt-size measurement contract with a deterministic, offline fixture
that reproduces the 2026-11-24 large-parent Phase 2 shape — **before** any
production change lands (TDD).

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-parent Phase 2 audit to
report the size of the exact prompt it sent, so a provider error on that shape
can be diagnosed without guessing or a live provider.

## Context / evidence

Parent item `SA-0MWV3N94G007H6A9`. The failing Phase 2 call was on
`RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI`: a parent with 14 children (all `completed`/`done`),
a ~18 KB description and 9 acceptance criteria. The failing runs persisted
`calls=2 parse_ok=1 provider_errors=1` with no prompt size recorded because
`_call_pi` reads `input_tokens` from the `agent_end` usage block, which a
`finish_reason: error` call may not emit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A deterministic offline fixture represents the failing shape: a parent
  with 14+ children carrying persisted audits, a ~18 KB description and 9+
  acceptance criteria. The fixture drives the **production**
  `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` prompt-construction path (the test must not
  re-implement prompt assembly).
- AC2 — A test asserts the measured Phase 2 parent prompt size (bytes and
  estimated tokens) is captured by production code and retrievable from the
  call result / per-call timing line / debug-log entry.
- AC3 — A test asserts the prompt size is still captured on a provider-error
  (`finish_reason: error`) path where the stream carries no `agent_end` usage
  block, so the failing prompt size is never lost.
- AC4 — The tests fail against the current implementation and pass once the
  measurement change (C3) lands, and they run in the audit test suite.
- AC5 — Capture the failure with measured size: the failing Phase 2 prompt shape
  is reproduced deterministically by a fixture (large parent: 14+ children with
  persisted audits, ~18 KB description, 9+ acceptance criteria) with the failing
  prompt's measured size recorded (bytes and estimated tokens), so the size
  hypothesis can be evaluated without a live provider.

## Minimal Implementation

None — this is the first, test-first slice.

A large-parent Phase 2 audit will report the exact measured prompt size, so a
provider error can be diagnosed from the log alone instead of guessing.
